The cross shaped maze in the ice area from Dragon Blazers. Once you go in it, no matter where you go, you'll always be brought back to the same room.

Normally one of the characters is supposed to guide you through the maze. But it became one of the most famous (or should I say infamous... XP) parts of the game because if you go there without that character, you'll get basically stuck... FOREVER.

The developers actually say something about this in the manual… It warns you this glitch is actually "one of the bad guy's magic spells"… Yeah XD... Sorry guys, I think you were just eating a little too much fruitcake when making this part of the game. XP

As a kid I had no idea that this was a glitch XD I literally spent hours on the screen wandering around thinking there was an exit!!

 

The thing is, there actually is one.

Somehow kid me was so stubborn, I think I went EVERY single possible direction somehow XD Then the last direction you go is up.

If you do that, you'll find a door that doesn't appear ANYWHERE else in the game.

This shocked me so much as a kid I screamed and pulled my controller so hard it unplugged the console XD I actually started crying… but I knew my mom would turn off the game if she heard me, so I held my breath and started hiccuping and gasping. I literally thought I was going to choke on my tears. It only made me cry more that I had to plug the game back in by myself. I was so scared that I would get electrocuted and die from the wires. I was actually always afraid of electrical sockets too because I thought they were looking at me XD (Come on I wasn't a weird kid I promise... XP I got over it after that)

So I started the game again, and with my hands shaking I went back into the maze.

But what's super weird, was that somehow, I was able to get RIGHT back to the door.

I was so happy I almosted started screaming again, but remembered to hold my breath halfway XD Now I was going to be able to see what was in the secret door…

Or so I thought XP It was locked. And I've never been able to find ANY key in the game that opens it.

Since then, I can actually get to the door pretty consistently if I concentrate.

Unfortunately I don't know exactly what I'm doing, and it feels different every time, so I can't give any advice XD

stories.author: @SlimeWizaaard
stories.text:
I didn’t grow up in the 80s but my dad did, and he loved the original Zelda. And when I was around 9 my dad and step mom got one of those unofficial consoles that could play old games. With it they got Mario 1 and 2, Zelda 1 and 2, and a few other games. I think they played Zelda 1 the most, I did to and even got through the first dungeon by myself, but mostly I would watch them play. And one of my core memories with that was when my parents would get stuck trying to get through a dungeon and listening to the constantly looping dungeon music. It was almost hypnotic, and I would lose myself in the mournful digitized refrains. Until I could separate the layers of the song and focus on each one, until the song began to change in my head even though I knew it was the same, until it gave me a headache and I had to leave the room.

This song brought back those memories. I don’t even know if I registered it but I found myself entering that same state, that same trance as I did when I was 9. Amplified tenfold by the haunting context of where I was, of what I had to do. Of what I knew this represented. Tricky Tony is truly a master of his craft.

stories.author: @TheRealRELSAY
stories.text:
The two vessels sat- overlooking the vast, pixelated ocean. WHITE CLOAK glanced to her partner, HEROSWORD. 

They noticed her staring, and gave an affirmative nod, before reaching for their drink. 

They idly sipped, the waves crashing against the shoreline of their private hell. 

WHITE CLOAK simply held her own drink in her hands, miserably looking at her umpteenth cup of hot chocolate. Well, more like tepid chocolate, as her natural freezing touch made any beverage she held gradually chilled. 

Despite being given a respite from the SOUL forcing the pair onward, both knew that such pleasantries were rare and fleeting. 

The only thing that -Noelle- WHITE CLOAK remotely found positive about recovering the SOULS [redacted] was that she at least got to reconnect with -Kris- HEROSWORD. When they both weren’t being possessed and forced to kill darkners that is. 

She could only wonder if her awfully-wedded partner felt anything similar, as she could have sworn that she saw them looking over to her veiled face a few times and blushing ever so slightly. The thought warmed -Noelle- WHITE CLOAK, but only a little. 


Either way, they would be spending much more time with the other whether they truly wanted it this way or not. Why -Kris- HEROSWORD had dragged her all the way out to the beach made little sense in her frazzled mind, as it wasn’t like the SOUL couldn’t just rip them back to the edge of the next gameboard whenever it felt like it.
She had a shadow of a feeling that -Kris- felt similarly about the fake beach, and was only trying to do… anything different, to break up the usual monotony of… well. 

 
Why would it matter where they waited, when any semblance of leisure was shallow at best. Sooner or later… the SOUL would grow restless, dragging them both to angel knows where- their entire physical forms nothing but pieces on a wall for the parasite to pick at. 

…

Anyways, the beach, devoid of life as it was, offered only the faintest veneer of familiarity in her eyes- she was quite certain that -Kris- HEROSWORD could recall quite vividly memories of visiting the actual town beach with her, Azzy, and [REDACTED]. Oh how messily they all played, yet she still cherished their time nonetheless. Such fond memories only heightened how unbearably _false_ the current location felt. The beach -Kris- HEROSWORD had stopped them at was nothing more than a shallow imitation, and it made little difference. Soon, the SOUL would come for them both, and they would start up their now-routine song and dance. Ugh, if [REDACTED] heard how snobbish she was acting right now, she’d probably yell at them both.. she appreciated the gesture, she really did. It’s the thought that counts right? That’s what her father always told her whenever her mo- Carol would say she wasn’t putting 100% into her coloring homework. 
Compared to the lovely little excursion she was on now, watching her parents argue sounded goddamned serene. 


When did she become so cynical? It’s not like she was forced to be- wait, that isn’t true, LOL. “Like hell I was…” the hooded figure murmured to herself. There was no desire to paint this “adventure” as anything more than a twisted game of playing house. Still, the fact that she found herself being so… bitter about the whole situation still gave her a split second of pause- she really had become a new person hadn’t she? Or had the real her woken up? 

….


“What is even real at this point?”


-Kris- HEROSWORD said out loud. 

She glanced to them, their partner staring off into the blackened sky above as if they themselves had heard the question in her head. -Noelle- WHITE CLOAK thought upon their -friend- -lover- partner’s query for a moment, then whispered out her verdict. 

“I like to pretend that the connection we have is still real. It’s the only thing either of us get to keep after… everything we did…”

The beach. So wonderful. If she only had a camera. Tenna’s board had a camera, but no. The SOUL decided to throw the normal, happy, and safe game away so they could taste something _original._ 

“How f*cking quaint”, -Noelle- WHITE CLOAK dryly chuckled. 

She turned to look at her partner again, and HEROSWORD fidgeted in their seat. Then, unexpectedly, they leaned towards her and whispered into her ear. 


….


_“I’m sorry, __-Noelle.-__ “_



She sighed and gave them the most pathetically sad smile she’s ever given anyone (minus that one annoying classmate, what was his name again?)  though she doubted they could see her facial expression through the hood. What could they possibly be sorry for? It’s not like she was trying to fight back anymore, neither of them really were. Any and all pretenses of getting stronger had froze over and died several routes ago, they were pretty much just being using one another as dolls at this point. Compatible dolls, to be certain, but puppets forcibly embraced on the same red string. The worst part? She would be lying if she said she didn’t get a perverse thrill out of it. Making the _other_ person cower. Making the _other_ person cry. However -Kris- HEROSWORD felt about their wintery “joyride” was relative, as however bitter  might have been before, at least they didn’t have to suffer alone. She hoped Kris was having fun, at least a little. Surely doing all this, as beyond insanity it was… 

…Wasn’t it nice to reconnect again? 


Honestly, why should her childhood friend beat themselves up, even now? So they couldn’t protect her from that…. floating red…. thing.  At least they were on the same page now, and maybe now everyone would stop seeing her as just some victim to smother with “protection”.  She honestly hoped -Kris- HEROSWORD wasn’t still hung up about the incident on the couch, now that she understood the true nature of the SOUL, she firmly believed that it was only a matter of time that she was summoned as the “bride” to her long-suffering “groom.” As scary as it was, when did she never not like scary? Whether it be from them, Catti, [REDACTED], or… 

….Su- What was she talking about? Oh yes, her partner’s guilt. She didn’t resent them at all for it, not in the slightest. If anything, shouldn’t -Kris- be happier? They get to have her all to themselves, and now that they’ve both been ensnared, realistically they have nothing left to lose. Yes, -Kris- all to herself… though neither of them hardly felt like a prize… She glanced towards them again, -Kris- now slumped over in their beach chair with both hands covering the bottom of their face. Their piercing ruby eyes staring into nothingness, for what felt like a short eternity.

As fun as this “date” was…. she needed her “hero” with their head in the game, not in pixel clouds. She gently took her “partner” by their hand in her own, the thornring gripping into their palm. They winced at this, but made no effort to remove their hand. Apart of her wanted them to feel the sting, apart of her WANTED them to have even feel a fraction of the dull agony her hand feels every second of every day she spends wearing the stupid ring. -Kris- idly rubbed her thorny band with their index finger, almost in a perverse reverence. 
Must like the acute pains now, huh Kris? 
Her childhood friend, tormentor, and now “lover” a ruined masochist. 


Just like her. Some “good influence” she turned out to be. Surely, her [REDACTED] would be proud at how much of a “rebel” she was being. All it took was both her and her “protector” doing everything the damned parasite demanded, down to the last frosted letter. 


Before she could get another thought out, a bright flash of red light pierced the sky, followed by the unmistakable sound of the SOUL reconnecting into the game console. 


They both shuddered involuntarily, before straightening themselves out of their recliner chairs. 

HEROSWORD smiled miserably at her, before taking one final sip of their pixelated beverage. 

As she adjusted her ring, she saw the pulsating red terror slowly floating over to where they were on the ocean shore. The damned thing might as well have had a GPS shoved into it. 


Bracing themselves, they took each other’s arms in a twisted embrace, hugging each other one last time before they both went under. 

The SOUL was nearly on them now, the dark fountain on the horizon roaring at them, as if to say it had waited long enough. The dark fountain could wait apparently, as the SOUL had nothing better to do than “play house” with the two of them. 

The frigid waves crashed down upon the shore as if Heaven itself was raging at their sinful union. 

A massive whoosh was heard, as the Soul descended downward to yank them back up into the darkened heavens. It did *not* look happy, to say the least. HEROSWORD, sensing the impending takeover, closed their eyes, and took WHITECLOAK’S  hand tightly in theirs as they hugged. 



….




Leaning in, *Kris* whispered their final thought into *Noelle’s* ear. 

“If this is is ever over…. we need a real vacation.” 

*Noelle* could only smile though her shrouded cloak. “You’re buying the drinks then, Krismas.”

stories.author: @FelisDeNox
stories.text:
This is my favourite track of the game.


The way it's written, the way it fits in the secret game, the way the melody is made of repeating notes, only changing note order or octaves...
It makes me feel anxious. Dreadful. It reminds me of when I was a child, exploring bits on the internet I shouldn't be on. Seeing things I never imagined existed, things I wasn't supposed to know or see, at least not yet.
But it also feels like entrapment. The notes that keep repeating, it's like a loop, something you can never escape, which fits with the dungeon this theme plays on. The walls, the enemies, it makes you feel stuck. Like a prophecy. There is no way to change it or destroy it: your fate is written, and just now you realize that. That you never had a choice. That you're helpless. That you're just a pawn of time and space.
But, it also seems... strangely hopeful? The octaves shift from a lower to a higher pitch. Whoever showed you what you weren't supposed to see; your fate, is also showing a way to 'escape' it. To change it. Showing you another path.
Lastly, it has a ever so subtle hint of curiosity. A part of you is anxious about playing fate, but another part is looking forward to it. "What would happen if I...?". The question lingers in your mind, tempting you to proceed.
You don't know much about this "alternate" path you just found out. Nor what will happen if you try to cheat the prophecy. But one thing you know:

*The forbidden path began with ice magic.*

stories.author: @PetikG
stories.text:
For a side-quest that's advertised as Kris having fun playing games just as they remember, this is the most unsettling part of the chapter by far.

You are standing all by yourself in an unlit room, playing a game where you progress by killing several enemies, while once again being faced with the tough question of whether you are doing the right thing. Next you do what's told in many classic video game creepypastas and break out of bounds into an endless sea of palm trees.
Speaking of endless, the glacier's maze feels exactly like that. Like wherever you go doesn't matter and always leads back to the same spot. Accompany that with many hints to chapter 2's alternate route and with perhaps the most haunting chiptune track I've heard lately, the glacier maze makes you want to escape as soon as possible.

And even Kris themself is unnerved by this. You can tell by the moments when they flinch, or look away. Such as when you have to kill the two other party members in the game, or when you're approaching the dreaded shelter and they briefly refuse to come closer. Or when they step back once the game's character break the fourth wall.

As if that wasn't enough, when Susie arrives and you tell her you are having fun playing the game, she tells you not to be a tryhard by yourself, otherwise you'll end up like Berdly. Which does not sound so bad, if you don't discover it on the "weird route".

stories.author: @DementedDuskull
stories.text:
My two scents (*they smell like freshly rained grass and spicy pickled peppers...): The mysterious entity who drove both Jevil and Spamton crazy is the one who holds the ShadowMantle, who we'll just call Eram for convenience. We do not know their name; many thought it was Mike for a while, but that was a red herring. Eram talks to us for the first time HERE, which is huge, as they have largely hid in the shadows up until now, no pun intended. They seem to be connected to the cat-like, yellow and pink-eyed shadowy entity from Ralsei's story at the start of Chapter 3, and by extension the secret smiling yellow and pink-eyed face in Queen's Mansion Basement in Chapter 2, and the similar cat-like yellow and pink-eyed minions that the Shadow Mantle boss summons during the fight. So we _kind of_ know what they look like, but they are still shrouded in mystery. The way they're being set up reads almost as if they're some kind of god or ghostly being that haunts the Dark World as the metaphysical embodiment of shadow, "the fallen star, creating rivers from its tears". They made the Shadow Crystals (and the BitterTear item too, I guess), and then hid them around the Dark World for unknown purposes. 
They hid one in Card Castle, which Jevil already found. With the knowledge and power it brought, he correctly foretold to King that he would rise to power in The Knight's name, until Seam tricked Jevil into a cage and fled.
They hid another in the broken machine in Queen's Mansion Basement, and we even saw their face there as if they were watching and waiting for someone to grab it, which Spamton eventually does, to their delight.
The Roaring Knight already has a Shadow Crystal, which it could have obtained from TV World, but also possibly the Dark World in the Shelter. If not from TV World, then Eram's main meddling there is the hiding of the Shadow Mantle, meant specifically for Kris, who created this Dark World. When The Knight is beaten, a small shard is taken off of their blade. I'm reasonably sure this is supposed to represent the BlackShard weapon, not the Shadow Crystal, even though it says you picked up the Shadow Crystal first. Is The Knight's blade MADE of Shadow Crystals...? We don't know.
And finally, a Shadow Crystal was placed in the desk in The Old Man's study, clearly because Eram wanted him to find it, but The Old Man wasn't interested in a prophecy that looks the same from every angle, and didn't use it.
Seam implies there are only five Shadow Crystals, or at least only five that they know about. Overall, the character's actions and motives are greatly shrouded in mystery. Spamton makes me want to believe they're secretly a Lightner because of the garbage noise on the phone, but the amount of sway and control they have over reality in the Dark World has me wondering otherwise...

I don't remember when, but during a town segment in chapter 3 or 4, Susie mentions that she hears music across the lake.

Thinking of playing this game again some time. I was extremely excited for new chapters. Before one week of this game's release date, I hurried and finished the first two chapters to freshen my memory of the story and the game. But I liked the creator did experimented with the game and gave something new like that game inside game thing. I liked the ending of that chapter. 

I immediately started Chapter 4 to continue the story, I was at the edge of my seat. I played for 1-2 hours. Then, I waited till tomorrow and played for some time again. But I was itching to play more but I couldn't, since I didn't have time to play it for myself. So I opened YouTube and just started watching spoilers because I wanted to know what happens next in the story. It was amazing experience, Chapter 4 blew my mind. The final boss fight was really really cool. I like the friendship of Kris and Susie. 

I kinda stopped after that, I stopped loving playing games. It just didn't hit the same anymore, Deltarune reignited the flame but the flame didn't last long. I didn't bother to replay the game and find new secrets and contents. I have all the secret bosses, dialogues to encounter myself. It seems like I didn't do justice to this game. I have some very fun memories with Undertale and Deltarune (CH 1+2) games, so it really sucks that I just don't have the energy to enjoy these games like I want to.

Past the tacky Christmas cheer of the holiday manor lies the truth. Dess' room. Band posters, punk cds, all the hallmarks of teen rebellion perfectly preserved as if frozen in time. You shouldn't be in here, you know you shouldn't, but you cant help it. As you lightly step around the room, carefully as to not even disturb the thin layer of dust coating everything, you notice the wiffle bat in the corner. Bent, cracked, and dented, you can't help but wonder how many of those marks are from your head? Azzy's? Noelle's? You feel a lump grow in your throat. That one day you'll hear the front door opening and they'll walk back in. Knowing that something's wrong, but not having any closure... and don't even get me started on all of Dess' belongings that her family kept safely in her room. Seeing all her stuff... her guitar... rummaging through all the things she had... an unkempt bed, likely left the same way since the day she last got up from it... and with this track playing... man. It's almost like you can feel her bedroom waiting for her to come back, waiting for someone that'll never come home... just like Noelle...

How FUNNY would it be if the Dark World we discover while wandering around town during the festival was actually the PEZZA SHOP, right?

("Pink and gold" could also be another callback to the pink and yellow eyes of FRIEND). The Old Man also says "The vast garden is charred in an inferno of jealousy." Hmmm... The field is _charred,_ is it? Almost like...a PEZZA being cooked in the kiln? Asgore could even still be there, too.

stories.author: @gungy_vt
stories.text: As chilling as she is, I truly believe Carol is a red herring who knows about as much as Asgore does about what's going on, but gives off such bad vibes and negative charisma that she's easy to see as a villain. Sure, Kris definitely calls her to have her show up, that much is obvious, but I don't think the "police....sacrifice" call was Carol simply because of Kris wiping their phone's call history. Like, wiping the call history would be pointless if all the calls were made to the same number. On top of that, she has a corkboard in her room, meaning she's trying to piece together something. I believe her firing Asgore from the police was more a matter of keeping up appearances than trying to stop him from uncovering a truth. Like, whatever he did with the Shelter was too far for her to ignore without tanking her credibility as mayor, but she ultimately wants to know more just like he does. That's why she has a corkboard and lets him be late on rent and gives him extra work, etc. She's not in an alliance with the Knight, and probably isn't even aware of Kris's alliance. She's just got negative rizz and doesn't like someone she doesn't know going through Dess's stuff or possibly finding the code that's in the guitar. Her being okay with Kris might seem like an alliance, but you've gotta remember the Dreemurrs and Holidays are neighbors and friends; Susie is a new kid in town with an outward image of being a troublemaker. It makes sense Kris gets a pass while Susie doesn't.

stories.text:
I've noticed something strange in the music.
The motif at the start, the Spear of Justice motif, it plays 3 times.
You may be wondering, what's weird about that?
It's very unusual for Toby Fox, a melody plays very often 2 times, or two times then two more times with a change (back instrument added for example) so 4 times. (And often changing the very end to shake it up a little)
Almost NEVER in my memory 3 times, and each time it plays it changes (first is loud, second gets calmer, third gains an instrument), it's so weird. 

I think it is to fit with Gerson's idea of breaking the rules, the laid out path, and take your own. Symbolically, he doesn't apply to the given rule to make something new.
In his own word "Doubt, Irony, that's what poisons your story...
That, and too much predictability."

stories.author: @deltasrevenant
stories.text:
[Within the old ruins, Frisk stumbles upon a familiar old man... reading some books in a long forgotten place.]
* Hey there. Thought I'd take one last gander at this place. There were some old books I forgot... geh-heh.
* ...
* Y'know, it wasn't all written down quite right... our history. The pages changed, things got sanded down... and important things were forgotten... maybe on purpose.
* ...
* I never hated humans. Some of my best war buddies were humans... 'course, all of them are gone now. Long gone. 
* When they sealed us away, I didn't resist, much... the other side sacrificed a lot to get us down here. Rumor has it, it even used up all their magic... not sure though. I wasn't there. Geheheh.
* Humans and Monsters weren't always all enemies. No one really wanted to fight in that war... and the sides weren't really all that clear cut. 
* When the barrier was made... Old friendships were broken. Old business partners, lost... even some married couples, were...
* *I even knew one of the people doing the sealing. Heheh. Seein' them in that beautiful magician outfit, for the first time... for the last time, and at such a moment... It felt strange, I tell ya. Geheheheh...*
* ...
* But now, we're going back. ...Even if Humans accept us... Ya can't say everything will go smoothly. Asgore probably didn't believe that, either... until he met you. G'job, sprout.
* Geheheheheh!

(From the UNDERTALE 10th Anniversary Stream! Thank you, Toby. 🧡)

He's never directly name dropped (like they never go "hey look it's Gerson Boom") but it is pretty easy to piece it together if it's your first playthrough.

stories.author: @SirRayveltal
stories.text:
Oh boy, trauma dump time.  I apologize in advance.

Susie has always been the character I relate to most in Deltarune.  While Chapter 3 definitely helped with that, Chapter 4 is what sealed the deal.

My grandfather passed away recently, and Susie's dynamic with Gerson was almost identical to mine and my granddad's.  He was such a smug smartass but he genuinely loved me and wanted to see me succeed.  When I said I wanted to be a voice actor, he was more supportive than anyone else.  Even at the end.  We think he knew he didn't have much time left.  He didn't tell us though.  He didn't tell me.  He didn't want to see us sad, even when he was on his death bed.  Gerson as a whole, and this track in particular, remind me of him so much it hurts.

With all that being said, thank you, Toby.  Thank you for reminding me of him.  Thank you for making this damn game.  These last few months have been the hardest of my life, and you helped alleviate that pain, and with Susie and Gerson's dynamic in chapter 4, you helped put me at ease, at least somewhat.

As for my grandfather...rest in peace, old man.  I love ya.

Update: My birthday was 2 weeks ago.  I just found an old birthday card from him in my dresser.  Here I go crying again lol

Also, thank you for your support, guys...seeing people show genuine sympathy and saying my comment actually impacted them to an extent too was so much more than I could have expected.

If you're going through something by any chance, I hope you know you're not alone.  Today, you all sure as hell proved to me that I'm not...thank you, guys.  :)

Edit 2: Gonna try to reply to everyone that I can.  Thank you so much for the support, again, guys.

Edit 3: Yesterday at the time of writing, my uncle just passed away, as well.  Wow life just has it out for me.

stories.author: @PROTOBLUES90
stories.text:
Saw a lot of myself in Susie. The shame, every fake friend, and it feeling like the world itself was out to get you. 
Then this crazy bastard came along. Spitting image of everything my grandfather ever was to me. 
A humble, dead legend. A father figure in all of the best ways, and a dear friend. 
Taking on Gerson and having him reteach me lessons I was taught so many years ago opened some old deep wounds, and it made it nearly impossible to finish the chapter with my friends afterwards. 

I knew who he was. I knew what this was. It never changed how any of it made me feel by the end. 
Hurt, smiling, and satisfied. 

If you are reading this Toby, Thank you. With every fiber of my being, thank you

stories.author: @thewhiteninjaminington8953
stories.text:
Gerson is my favorite Toby Fox character. By a lot. This song brings up all of these feelings every time. (rant incoming)

When I was playing chapter four, I was stunned by how attached I was to Gerson. He barely had half the screen time relative to his chapter when compared to Tenna or Queen, but he was still all I could think about when I finished the game. As I closed the game, I thought to myself about how much I hoped that Gerson would return to Castle Town and replace Malius as the smith. (I was kinda ticked that he didn’t have any new fusions.) I then pondered about how happy I would be just to see new dialogue with him and Susie. Heck, maybe he could even meet Alvin. I daydreamed about how he would uplift Seam’s nihilism, laugh with Lancer and Queen, beat up (and train) all the Darkners in the dojo, make a new smithy to give TopChef his dang bakery back, and so on and so on. That was when I was hit with the realization that I had walked right into Toby’s emotional bear trap. I wanted to see Gerson one last time just as much as Susie did. I didn’t want to say goodbye to a character I had waited years to see fleshed out from a humble shopkeeper. I wished he was alive. I wished he was real. He WAS real, to me. Everything about him was that of a real person, a man anyone would be lucky to have as their teacher. 

In summary… 
I don’t want to forget Gerson.
I don’t want to forget any of the Darkners. 
I… don’t want to forget anything or anyone in this game, lightner or darkner.
But more pressingly, I don’t want to see them go in the first place. 
Chapter 7 is going to be very hard on me.

Sorry if this is too sappy or overly emotional to take seriously.

stories.author: @fightingirl10
stories.text:
ok so I literally cried when I managed to win gerson's battle and he talked about perseverance (and overall about fighting destiny)

chapter 3 and 4 release happened to coincide with my very last chemo. I've been through an hell of an year (really felt his line about the world's spinning feeling like an insult), I was REALLY sick, then I got better but it was constant highs and lows, managing to adjust to side effects, trying to enjoy little things and then discovering new problems.
There was a time I thought my chances were very low and I would prefer knowing I had to die rather than dealing with uncertainty. 

Then one day I woke up. Something clicked. I said "I don't want this". I insisted in getting a 2nd opinion for surgery.
It was complex, I got pelvis bone resection, muscles cut and rearranged, and I've been doing physical therapy for months.
I'm afraid to say this out loud, but the tumor's gone. I'm in remission and have scans every three months.

I couldn't breathe, then I got up.
I couldn't lift my leg, now I walk
"Each time, you get a little better."

Afterwards, I saw my artist pals bringing to life their characters in beautiful detail in that sprite section. I was going to comment that I felt kind of bad that my drawing was so amateurish compared to theirs, but when I was about to type those words out, Gerson's words to Susie came to mind.

"As long as you got the point, the words don't matter"

I stopped myself from typing that self-defeating comment right there, feeling warmth over the encouraging words of this wonderful fictional old coot.

Thanks Toby. You and your team are creating something wonderful and inspiring 💚

stories.author: @velocijammer1454
stories.text: I’ve struggled with addiction for a long time. I won’t specify the type. I’ll just say it wasn’t dr**s or alc*h*l I’ve wanted to be better but kept finding myself coming back to that escape because I always felt alone. Guess I adopted a sense of fatalism. I admit over the years I let myself go. For awhile every night was just another hopeless night. Letting myself be brainwashed by whatever was in front of me in the dark. Then I listened to an old man’s wise words. And I remembered that little white pen called “hope”. I remembered something I’d almost forgotten. That no matter what we do to ourselves. No matter what anyone does to us. No matter how hard the world tries to brainwash us or kick us down. We all have that same fire in our eyes. Even if we can’t always see it. We can all be as free as Gerson if we wanted to be. We just need to fight for that freedom everyday. To fight against what’s holding us down. And break away. Maybe I’ll just spiral again. Maybe I won’t. But I’ll tell you this: I’m never gonna stop fighting to be human.

stories.author: @Pascal77ALT
stories.text:
"It's funny... there was a time when they were coming over almost every day.
 We'd play, and we'd play... then after a while, they would suddenly get very still, like they were remembering something.
They'd go into the dining room to "get a snack," then after a few moments, I'd hear the piano.
The first few times, I went into watch them play, but when they realized I was looking, they'd always shut the piano and come back.
So over time, I just started staying on the couch in the living room. I'd lie there, listening to them play, sometimes for hours, sometimes even until I fell asleep.
Even then, what were they thinking about me?
Maybe they weren't thinking about me at all.
They didn't have a piano at their house, so they probably just came over to use mine.
Even then, with my eyes open, there were times when I wasn't even sure if we were friends.
But when I closed my eyes,
it felt like a concert just for me."

stories.author: @q5uzxy-wl3md
stories.text: Every time I hear this song, I picture an animation, but since I can't draw, the idea stays only in my head. I’d like the first part of the song to show just Kris playing the piano—with something to fill the space, like showing the setting and so on—but then it would cut to an image of blue skies being swept over by Spamton’s hand against the wall (as if he were painting over the sky—you know, painting the background we see in his shop), focusing on Kris playing and Spamton painting with his hands in a very free, loose style. From the 0:33 mark, there would be a wide shot of Kris playing—now with the red soul-control lines clearly visible—followed by a final scene of Spamton’s hand sliding down the wall, stained with paint as he sits down looking somewhat sad and melancholic, with his green strings also clearly visible. After all, that small act of joyful defiance had led nowhere; it didn't matter—they remained puppets. Thank if you read all of this. And if anyone wants to animate this (which I find unlikely), I’d be happy to see it, and I’d appreciate it if you could credit me, please.

stories.author: @lordhocageroblox
stories.text:
One of the last things my best friend turned brother and I experience was Deltarune. We finished chapter four just about two weeks before his passing. Gerson was his favorite character out of the entire game, that goofy turtle old man made him so happy every time he showed up and his boss fight was by far his favorite secret boss. It's an odd mixture of sadness and happiness hearing this song now, but all the same... Thank you, Toby. For all the memories. Between Undertale and Deltarune, you gave a man who could barely leave his home after a hard fight with Cancer a break from reality and how harsh it can be. 
Every moment those games provided was like fresh air to he and I, all the crazy fights and feats, all the goofy comedy breaks, and even the moment he got spooked by one of Spamton's shop dialogues (He named his file Mike). Everything in your games felt like an adventure, the kind he didn't get to have many of. 
You might not care, and you definitely didn't know him, so I don't expect any response about his passing... I just felt like it had to be said how grateful Michael was for every experience you helped make for us. 
8/24/96-7/29/25. God Rest him.

stories.author: @Shadowiser82Official
stories.text:
I see all the comments here including Undertale AND Deltarune in here, and thought I'd say my piece cuz I've really enjoyed both games and I'm a bit of a theorizing nerd lol.

I was never a huge fan of Gerson. Seeing him in Chapter 4 certainly surprised me because it wasn't a character I expected Toby to bring to the table. He was just a Shop NPC in Undertale, after all. I expected him to be the wise tutor character after seeing how he helped Susie post-Jackenstien fight...and then I reached pre-Titan fight.

Where Gerson challenged Susie. With the awfully familiar spear pattern attacks, and the familiar Battle of A True Hero motif in the battle theme, my perspective of him changed entirely. He wasn't just an old turtle, he was a full-on seasoned battle veteran. I still haven't beat him (neither the Titan, but that's neither here nor there), and realized that despite how old he is, he's still in his prime lol. After all, a turtle's lifespan can be anywhere from 10 - 150+ years (depending on species) and Gerson is anything but slow.

Then someone in the comments mentioned that Gerson (Undertale) said that we couldn't kill him. And, in Undertale, that is true. Why would you kill someone who is selling you stuff that helps you get stronger? All the shop NPCs knew that, they knew they were safe as long as they provided Frisk/the Player with what they wanted. It makes me wonder if Gerson was just as strong in Undertale as he was in Deltarune, but he chose to be a shop NPC because it was simply easier and/or smarter.

Even in the pacifist route, Gerson was a bit different from the other shop NPCs. He was very smart and knew a lot about the Underground's history, all those plaques were placed throughout the Waterfall area, too. He was just as knowledgeable in Deltarune as he is in Undertale, the only difference is that Gerson had passed away from old age (his grave is located next to the Church in Hometown).

Small side note/theory, Toby said that Deltarune is neither the same universe Undertale is in, nor an AU of it. At first, I thought that maybe Deltarune was Undertale but in the future, after all the monsters finally got to the surface. But then I remember that Deltarune ≠ Undertale. And then I realized something: Undertale was made by Toby for fun. He wasn't expecting it to get as big as he did, he just made the game for his own enjoyment. And then it hit me, Deltarune was one of two possibilities: Deltarune is Toby's ideal revamp/ideal form of Undertale, OR he included Undertale characters in Deltarune because he knew it would bring all the Undertale fans in (and therefore more money, basically a very effective marketing strategy).

Okay, I've said my piece. If you read all this, congrats. Here's a treat for your hard work 🍫☺

stories.author: @exiist.mp4
stories.text:
The way Toby incorporates the freedom motif into these themes is so interesting. In The World Revolving, it’s almost the centerpiece of the song. Jevil doesn’t really have anything other than his idea of freedom, and he’s obsessed with it, so naturally it sorta takes over his theme.

In BIG SHOT, the motif is somewhat somber, a contrast to the bombastic energy in the rest of the song. Spamton is desperately trying to BECOME free, so the motif has more of a longing emotion. 

Gerson meanwhile, doesn’t really seem to care about his freedom. Rather, he’s free BECAUSE he doesn’t care about the “freedom” the knight is offering. As such, the motif is sorta tacked onto the end, like an afterthought. It’s also the first time that the motif is given some of variation, literally spelling out the fact that his freedom is different from the rest in musical form. Gerson’s freedom isn’t something that affects everything he does. Gerson’s freedom is REAL.

I could be wrong about all of this, I’m no mind reader after all, but part of the joy of music is the variety of ways it can be interpreted, right? Toby is phenomenal at creating music that tells a story, and I think that’s pretty neat :)

As a kid, I lived in a tiny town in the middle of a vast and empty prairie. 
Many of the buildings like the library, church, school and town hall were never locked, and I spent a lot of my nights just walking in through the front door of those buildings and just looking around at things in the dark. There were all manner of trinkets, baubles and doodads that I had no idea what they were. I would spend hours just looking at things, wondering what they were and what they were used for, or just making things up in my head. I remember the furnace in the deepest part of the basement became a growling mechanical beast, and the golden statues in the trophy case became the heroes who banished it. The empty gymnasium became a vast, sunless desert, the library an endless maze, the hallways neverending portals to unfamiliar places. I knew I shouldn't be there, so I never brought a flashlight. 

This really brings to mind those days.
My own little dark world...

stories.author: @thingymajik
stories.text:
Guys, Dess is dead.

Dess is the Knight.
And there is a cult.

Think about it, ASGORE has a shard, only received by the KNIGHT or those who have met the Roaring Knight.

And ASGORE left the police force presumably after Dess’ disappearance.

Out of GUILT.

If UNDYNE knows the code to the bunker, so would ASGORE too; as they are/were the chief of police.

ASGORE, out of GUILT of Dess’ disappearance, joined Carol to open fountains to bring back Dess.

Ralsei said that Specific but also SIMILAR fountains can bring back dead people.

So, if one person opens a Dark Fountain, and throws Dess’ remains into the fountain… They would create Dess in the Dark World; the ROARING KNIGHT.

Think about this, this is why the Knight is trying to bring the ROARING- To RESURRECT ITSELF.

By covering all in darkness, the Knight will roam FREE. FOREVER.

Also, the bat in Dess’ room and the guitar.

Carol uses the guitar for the Bunker’s code. “1225”.

Dess’ BIRTHDAY and NAME.

December Holiday. Christmas, Krissmas.

Kris is working with the Roaring Knight. That’s why Kris is welcome in Carol’s house, always. Same with Asgore himself.

They both are working with the Knight and are trying to make the SOUL oblivious to the CODE to the bunker, to stop Susie from getting in and cornering the KNIGHT.

Also, some say “if Dess is dead, then how is UNDYNE dragged to the Bunker???”

Well, it wasn’t Dess. It was someone else.

Someone young, fruitful, and Strong.

ASRIEL Dreemur.

This is a stretch, but Asriel could be overcome by Grief of Dess’ death, joining Carol in her quest to revive Dess. Refusing to let her go.

Trying to *find her* in infinite Darkness; Death.

Death. Somewhere dark, yet Darker. An unknown concept. Unexplored territory.

And who do we meet upon death? GASTER.

Or who we assume is Gaster.

Gaster is the fear of DEATH. The man on the other side.

Like the other side of the tree.

An Egg; a quite fragile object, but on the inside, it’s hollow and simple- you’re dead. And you can’t change that.

And this is why Dess stays Dead.

You cannot bring back someone lost to the dark.

Back to Dess’ room.

The beaten up baseball bat? That’s the Roaring Knight.

We know that Gerson is made from the hammer and his own ashes.

So Dess may be made from her Bat and HER ashes.

“Raise Up Your Bat” is about Dess. And the Knight’s SWORD looks like a Bat.

That’s Dess’ weapon, her old bat.

The Knight turns into a baseball upon going into ball form. One you would hit with a BAT.

Dess is the Roaring Knight, but she just can’t leave the Dark World without instantly disappearing back into pure darkness.

So someone waited outside Kris’ house, for Toriel.

But Dess gave them UNDYNE instead, as a sacrifice. To “make you stronger” upon slaying in the Dark World.

The stronger you are, the more efficient you are.

Meaning, Not even Susie can stop you when you open a fountain.

(I am the Yappatron)

Also, the voice on the phone to Kris.

The cult.

But it is only Carol talking: “You promised” *to bring her back, to FIND HER.*

“I’ll be back.” *To STOP SUSIE.*

The only question to be answered..? HOW and WHO (may have) has Dess died (to)…?


If you’re down here, thanks for reading this- I yap a LOT.

This is just my theory. If there are any problems or plot holes- Feel Free to point them out!!!

I’d do that often because I was a strange kid. I’d go downstairs and creep outside to stargaze, or climb trees, or hide under bushes and take delight in the fact nobody knew I was there. I’d pretend everyone else had vanished and I was the last person on Earth.
This song sounds like seeing my siblings tangled up on the couch, asleep while the main menu of a rental DVD loops on the TV (an old CRT, in fact).
It sounds like crossing paths with the neighborhood stray cat and silently passing one another by.
Sounds like the mysticism of childhood :)

stories.author: @YapYar
stories.text:
You know how Susie's eyes briefly light up red the same way Kris's do in the animation where she creates a dark fountain? What if the red eyes aren't just a thing Kris has purely for their creep factor? What if the red glow is the glow of _determination?_ As Queen explained, you need determination to open a fountain, and in the Deltarune world, all lightners possess the power of determination, not just humans, thus Susie is able to muster up enough determination to tear open a fountain.
...And for a brief moment, as she hovers at the apogee of her leap, knife raised in hand,

_a glimmer of red shines in her eyes._

"At last, LOVE finds it's way to the girl."
[An image depicting the girl and a heart shaped object in the middle.]
Not saying Susie is gonna become a new vessel, but that would be badass and totally in character for her to immediately and joyfully offer to take Kris's role once she finds out the truth about them and us, if it means Kris can be freed and she can fight the Knight solo and savescum endlessly until she beats them through pure practice and perserverance.

The girl is probably a supposed to be a fourth hero like Noelle or Dess though, since "And last, was the girl. At last was the girl" depicts the Rude buster, an actual symbol for Susie, while that other tapestry depicts a completely different character wielding a sword instead of an axe, but it's not like we were following the prophecy too closely anyways, what with us apparently HAVING THE WRONG HERO IN OUR PARTY FOR MORE THAN HALF OF THE LEGEND. Ralsei must not have seen that particular picture and still thinks Susie is the right hero, otherwise, he probably wouldn't have said "nothing changed" by the time we reached this point of the legend. Um, yes it has? This purple beast is on our team even though we were apparently supposed to defeat her and move on all the way back in ch1 and she's making everything better. 

I'd say the prophecy is already on track for being rewritten by the pen of hope. The first 4 chapters sure were!

The shattered prophecy states such, the humans soul must be sacrificed to give power to another.

This is the second hero of Deltarune.

stories.text:
I think it's about time I share my story I had with this Boss:
The first time I played through Chapter 4, I didn't get to the Secret Gerson Fight in the First Sanctuary, so I wasn't familiar with Armored Gerson until the end of the game. When Susie made her own Dark Fountain and I reached this Boss, I didn't think that Shadow Armored Figure was Gerson, I thought Susie was just being naive. I thought they were either a New Character or possibly Undyne for whatever reason. I had no idea at the time as it was one of the few bosses I came into completely spoiler free, but the music really gave off the impression that something was wrong. I struggled fighting them and before I got to the end of the fight, I thought this was going to be one of the hardest bosses in the game, even thinking this might've been an "optional" boss in a similar way the Roaring Knight is (Of course it's not unless you're using a glitch), all I knew at the time was that I HAD to push my way through this Boss fight if I wanted to find out what was going on, so I did just that. I HAD TO KNOW who we were facing! I felt bad for poor Susie during this because she didn't even want to fight them as she thought it was the Old Man. Even though I didn't spend much time with the Old Man, I already started to miss him. Like a famous saying goes, you don't know what you had until it's gone. Then, Susie used her healing move, which then illuminated the Dark Figure, but it went by pretty fast to where I was left confused, and then Ralsei finally shows up and SHATTERS THEM???   : 0
Ralsei then tells Susie that they're not Gerson and that it may have been a Statue in Gerson's Study that came to life from Susie making the fountain, but I'm still unsure to this day on what the deal with that Boss was, and I'm unsure on why Ralsei destroyed them when Ralsei is almost always very chill with all the monsters, including Big Bads like Chaos King, Spamton, the Roaring Knight, and even to some extent the Titan Spawns.
The weirdest part though is that this Boss is never brought up again in the game afterword, they're just kind of forgotten about. I do hope this "Character" comes back in some way or gets brought up again in Chapter 5, but only time will tell.

stories.author: @YapYar
stories.text:
Looking back on this fight, how emotionless and violent the statue was, and how Ralsei didn't even try to show it mecy...

What Ralsei said about the Titan later in the chapter comes to mind. "It's the fear-of-dark, the bump in the night. The shadow in the back of your mind. It has no emotions. It only exists to destroy." The Gerson statue was found in one of the dark labyrinths, which in itself formed in Gerson's study.
My theory is that those dark zones in both the 1st and 2nd sanctuary represent pure, unshaped darkness from the fountain, and manifest when the lightner creating the fountain doesn't have enough thoughts to manifest a concrete idea of what a person or place is supposed to be, so an unshaped, barren void is left in place, and then shaped, not by the lightner, but by the forces that dwell within the darkness itself.
Susie didn't know enough about Gerson to truly bring him back in her dark world, so the part of the world where his study used to be was left unfinished, and... raw.
The fireplace has gone out, this place is empty, barren,
_dark._


Same reason why Jackington's fight uses the Titan's mechanics. A Titan is the fear of dark given form, while Jack is a Halloween decoration, which is a celebration of fear and spooks, so he wields a weaker version of the Titan's powers.

stories.author: @flightarrowbear
stories.text:
I know no one will really see this, but I'd like a place to tell my story. I finished Chapter 4 basically right before I went through some stuff last year. This song always struck me as one of reflection and of loss, both in context of everything that awaits us in game, but also to past me. Looking back on everything so far, I see a lot of myself in Ch. 4 Susie. Perhaps it was because, in the end, we both lost a beloved mentor.
My high school choir teacher had terminal brain cancer, and passed away from it in October. I made two flights back to my home state to see him, the first to visit him in the hospital while he was still alive, and the second three months later for his memorial. I didn't get to see him during the first trip, and the hospital told me to leave when I couldn't get a hold of him. I also wrote him a card, but I never got the chance to give it to him. I listened to this song for hours in the hotel that trip, devastated. My one shot to say "thank you" was wasted. I was angry with him for a time, but I also know he was suffering. I don't hold it against him. At the very least, I don't ever regret trying.
Right at the start of my second trip, I heard this song again in the car. I hadn't heard it much since the first trip, so it hit me very hard while I drove in the dark for my 5AM flight. It was a reminder of everything I never got to say, and all the gratitude I never got to show him. I was in choir for six years while I was in school, and he was my teacher for four. I was also a shy kid and really blended in with the crowd, but singing became the thing I lived for during those brutal school years. He was an amazing teacher; we preformed some really challenging pieces for a high school level, and he really made us think about what we were actually doing and saying when we made music. He was the reason I really began pushing myself to get better at singing. Heck, I even got some solos and advanced to the top chamber choir in senior year! I did it for me back then, but I also did it to show that I was someone who deeply cared about the same thing he did; making music. I still heavily regret not getting to know him more. I still wish I got to tell him the impact he had on me. Instead of it being a reminder of that first trip, this time, it was like the music itself was acknowledging his passing.
So many of his students showed up to that memorial. I hadn't been to many in my life, admittedly, and they weren't for people I really knew. From what I'd been taught, funerals were usually serious and somber occasions, but this was our choir teacher we were talking about, so this wasn't an ordinary memorial in any sense of the word. There was so much more laughter than I'd expected. In another twist, the service was also a concert. Our programs had sheet music in them so we could sing with him one last time. His wife sang the solo of one of his favorite pieces. It was emotional whiplash at times, going from a beautiful speech about how much he is missed, to singing his favorite, lighthearted drinking song after every single speech, but that was just like him. I cried the entire service, even while I sight-read sheet music alongside my fellow musicians again for the first time in about 6 years.
I'd never really been one to believe in Heaven. But knowing how many lives he'd impacted, and remembering the beauty he'd brought into the world just by being himself, I believe in his Heaven. I believe that he arrived there with a giant smile on his face, and that he's up there right now singing in a choir with his fellow musicians. And to those of us still here on Earth, we can take care of passing on the torch of music for him. I'm not one of the folks who decided to become a music educator just like him, or preform professionally, but every time I sing an old song of ours from school or choir camp, I remember him. I still do our vocal warmups when I can, and I will never stop singing or loving music. His lessons are with me forever.
It's still hard for me to hear this song every time it gets shuffled into my Deltarune playlists. Time feels like it stops, just like it did that dark morning I drove to the airport, and I'm reminded that I still have the card I wrote for him, unopened. This song forces me to reflect on my regrets, but also reminds me to live life as boldly and happily as he did.
I hope you're having fun singing up there, Mr. Graham, for there must be a heaven if you are no longer here.

stories.author: @AKablalik
stories.text:
The entirety of Chapters 3 and 4 up until this point had felt like a mental confrontation with myself. For a long time, I have hated myself, hated the mistakes I’ve made, and have desperately wanted to do better, to break out of my comfort zone. 

Deltarune was part of my comfort zone back in 2021, but now that I’m almost a young adult, with so many friendships abandoned, obligations feeling suffocating, and my life changing, yet simultaneously not changing. I was sitting there, watching Ralsei break down, and I asked myself, “What happened to me?” I should be happy, but I’m not. This fantasy can’t comfort me anymore and maybe that’s for the better. 

I’m scared to play Chapter 5 when it comes out, because I don’t want to confront myself again. Maybe by that point I feel better but right now, I feel discontent. I want to truly smile again, but I feel as if that person doesn’t exist anymore, he grew up too fast…

stories.author: @RioXTorres
stories.text:
The song 12am plays when kris and susie are in the light world church in the rain. It's a very somber thoughtful song and works well with the heavy downpour outside the church.

Listen to that one if you don't remember it, and then go back here.

But 13am is much more fascinating to me because not only does it fit the two scenes it plays in REALLY well, but clocks do not count past 12 in standard North American time systems. Branching over into uncharted territory that was never supposed to exist. Bringing life and meaning to the unreal and hypothetical, stretching the concept of time out further than it was built to, resulting in a song that has mostly forgotten it's identity, pausing to quietly weep in its confusion and sadness, drifting away, feeling a sense of dread as it looses grip of each thought it thinks. Eventually forgetting to be a song. It no longer has the strength, nor the energy to find it's way back into continuity and purpose.

Like pouring water on a painting and watching all of the intricate details and emotions wash away in a downward motion. Smearing together daffodils, willow trees, and the beautiful mistress in the center, causing her eyes and mouth to look unnerving or ghostly, but at the same time conveying the emotion of terror in losing one's self.

The painting clearly does not like this death, neither does 13am.

stories.author: @noob-1928
stories.text:
Poor Ralsei. He's now my favorite character in all of DELTARUNE with how badly I can empathize with him.

When you decide that your worth can only be weighed in how happy you make everyone else, you'll find yourself with a loss of identity very quickly. You'll realize that sharing any of your worries will detract from the constant stream of affection you wish to be. And so you'll shut yourself away, faintly content with the idea that, even if you're suffering deep down, no one will know. And that gives you a little bit of hope, because why should anyone be as miserable as you?

No one should be, Ralsei. And that includes you, too. Speaking from personal experience, it includes all of us.

A shared joy is double a joy. A shared misery is but half a misery. So always remember, no matter how tough it gets, that it's okay not to smile sometimes. Because it's always easier to smile when you're not the only one who can tell if it's genuine.

stories.author: @Redka_poq
stories.text:
I can't properly express my thoughts on all of this because I'm not a musician and I don't have the knowledge to describe here why this melody is so amazing. BUT

I want to say that every time, hearing new tracks from Toby Fox, I feel like I understand why I admire art so much, why I love music so much, why I am delighted with the emotions I get from listening to different songs/looking at completely different works of art. I see the amazing things people can do when they open their hearts to their dreams and desires. Toby Fox's music once again feels like the quintessence of everything creative and spiritual. 

 It is clear that Toby is a musician. Music is his weapon and his true passion. You can feel this great love for everything he does in his heart, which he shares with those around him. And that's why, I think, everything Toby does so easily resonates in people's souls and inspires them to start creating on their own. 

Listening to this music, it's as if I can't think about anything except the music itself. I just fall out of the world for a couple of minutes, not immersing myself in memories or my fantasies, but dissolving in the music itself without any ulterior motives. I just live this melody. And so it is with everything to me that Toby does.
 He gives himself completely to this, which makes you simply feel his passion and love, relating them to yourself and the desire to express your emotions, your passion, your love just as brightly and clearly.
Thank you, Toby.

"Did you know...?" she inquired, the red ink of fate dripping from her wrist, staining the window of destiny on the ground.

"...yes..."

stories.author: @Eloraic
stories.text:
Genuinely, I'm not one for tears. I've never cried to a video game before.

This ALMOST changed that. Almost, meaning I was on the floor, hand covering my mouth and genuinely in shock at this.

The moment I saw Kris's health hit 1, I thought I was doing something wrong, and desperately tried to move to SOME sort of safe-pixel spot,

Then Susie took the blow, and it clicked. I had to keep going. 

Blow, after blow, Susie got knocked down to 1 HP.

Then, At the end of her line, Ralsei took the blunt of the blow. Fragile, flimsy Ralsei.

I was actively choking as they kept pushing on despite being on death's door, ensuring that none of them would open it if the other could help it.

This was the moment I knew this wasn’t just a follow up to Undertale from a guy who wasn’t done making games, but a masterpiece in the making all on its own merits, from a guy with a hell of a story to tell.

stories.author: @-lite-
stories.text:
Damn, once again I’m convinced that Toby is an absolute genius when it comes to music. I mean seriously, what he did in GUARDIAN is absolute cinema. Back in Undertale, the soundtrack was great and genius because all the music was connected.
But in Deltarune, it’s on a whole new level — the games themselves are musically connected. Not directly, of course, but you can clearly hear it.

Just think about it — why does the boss theme feel like a final boss track, not just a mid-game one?
The answer’s actually pretty simple, and it lies in the part starting at 0:54.
That section is literally built almost identically to Finale from Undertale — same music box, same bells. And on top of that, the whole thing is riding on an amen break — just like Finale did (and yeah, obviously GUARDIAN is basically Burn in Despair 2.0).
Also, I love how Toby plays with leitmotif progression:
In Undertale, the Once Upon a Time theme evolves into Hopes and Dreams.

And in Deltarune, Beginning / The Legend literally evolves into the goddamn GUARDIAN — and that’s potentially not even the peak yet. 

You can literally hear how Susie, Kris, and Ralsei go from the goofy trio who are “destined to save the world” into a team of true heroes standing against the darkness itself — regardless of how grand or terrifying it is.

It’s another year. Another year, that is if you’re not lying on your deathbed.

Your vision is blurry. The people around you feels like an anomaly.

Suddenly, the small one picks a conversation. “Grandpa? Ar y” That was all that could’ve been heard. You lost the ability to write your own name a long time ago.

Another voice lingers in the room. For some reason, for some odd reason… you heard it.

“Dad, what do you think of your life? Do you even have your last wish before you go?”

You can feel your lips shaking. Without warning, three words mutter from your mouth. You can’t control it. You can’t control anything. Your hopes and your dreams conclude here. It seems like your journey has came to an end.

“Think I’m old.”

Suddenly, consiousness hits. You don’t know what is happening. You can never know.

Except, you are.

Something from your childhood enlightened your already decaying neurons. Streads that can’t even control who you are when this is finally over.

You try to silence it off. It is still there. You feel lucid, but for some reason, you smiled. They say you are never going to smile again. Yet you did it.

The air crackles. Frankly, you feel a sense of freedom. And a migraine coming on…

You closed your eyes, not knowing it would be the last time. Again, the concept of knowledge has been voided long ago.

Your smile fades away.

stories.author: @S1lv3r1
stories.text:
This moment really got me.

Undertale was the first non-platformer game I ever played. I was obsessed with Mario, Sonic, and Kirby as a kid. In terms of other types of games, they just didn't interest me. I remember watching my dad play Paper Mario, but it looked overwhelming. 

When I was 13 I saw a YouTube clip of Jacksepticeye fighting papyrus, saw the blue soul, and thought Undertale was a platformer game, so I decided to try it out.

I remember getting stuck in Ruins, and then getting lost in Snowdin because there was more than one exit on some of the screens. It was... Frustrating. There was no clear end goal in mind, no collectibles, powerups, menus, lots of text, it was all so foreign. But I kept playing anyway, since there was something so charming to me about the game. I liked the characters, the music, the humor.

I remember the first time I made it to the MTT hotel scene with Sans and It's Raining Somewhere Else played. I remember "You'd be dead where you stand" and how much it intrigued me. Despite how much the game frustrated me because it was unfamiliar, I was enamored with everything it had to offer.

I eventually went on to finish the game, as well as the Genocide route even though Undyne and Sans took me probably like a month to beat cumulatively. Undertale ended up being my favorite game of all time.

After finishing the game, I decided to branch out, try some things other than platformers. Adventure games, Metroidvanias, Roguelikes, JRPGs, Visual Novels, you name it. Undertale opened my eyes to the world of gaming at large.

Fast forward to today, I'm turning 22 next month, I'm in college, I'm working full time, I'm a completely different person. I got a day off at work specifically for when chapters 3 and 4 dropped so I could play them. After spending all day on the game, finally getting back to the overworld in chapter 4, 1 AM, this song plays. 

I can't quite describe the feeling I got when that first piano chord struck. I don't believe nostalgia has ever made me tear up before. It was a unique experience, to say the least. I just sat there in stunned silence, my mind swirled with memories good and bad, old memories and recent ones, and I just thought about how much time has passed.

The self reflecting of growing up, the friendships I've made and the ones that have faded with time, the mistakes I've grown from, the ones that haunt me, the effort I've put into myself and my life.

Laughter, crying, smiling, screaming, running away, finding home again. 

An angry drive, a smack to the steering wheel that your wrist regrets the next day, a job you stayed at longer than you should have.

A long conversation- hundreds of miles from home under the dimly lit parking lot at 4 AM when you know you should have been in bed hours ago.

The gentle rain tapping against the windshield, the return journey as you blast the freezing cold AC at your face, the bittersweet air just barely keeping you awake as the bright yellow lines of the road become a blur.

And it all comes rushing back from a single piano chord. That little boy with a barely functioning laptop. That little boy playing Undertale. That little song about the rain.

I can't wait to hear it again.

stories.author: @sunsflwrs
stories.text:
i want to try to put what this track meant to me into words. even if nobody reads it, even if i make typos because i'm feeling too much and because i can't see through my tears, i want to get this out there somewhere. ever since i finished chapter 4 this morning, ever since i heard this track - i can't stop thinking about how lucky i am. i think it's truly something special to love a piece of media as much as i feel like i do, i really hope that everyone out there has something they love as much as i love undertale and deltarune because i feel like nothing else compares. 

i think i first played the game in 2016 after getting into the fandom at 2015, i was ten years old. it met me at a time in my life where i was going through a lot of growth, discovering things about myself and my family. i give undertale a lot of credit when it comes to helping me realize my queer identity, i had never really considered the thought until i saw undyne and alphys. beyond that, the story resonated with me so deeply and i don't really understand why. i was 10, i missed a lot of things, i misunderstood a lot of things, but it quickly developed into an obsession. growing up neurodivergent, i had a tendency to bring up my interests TOO much, and it led to me being outcasted and its given me a hesitance to talk about the things i love to this day.

but with undertale, something weird happened. every person i recommended it to that gave it a try felt the same way about it as i did. a friend of a friend even ended up getting an undertale tattoo, and it's weird to know it was a butterfly effect caused by my recommendation.

i fully allowed myself to be consumed by this game for two years, before i began feeling a lot of shame. i was the weird girl in middle school in a southern conservative town, everyone else had these normal interests and i didn't, and i just - tried not to focus on undertale for a while.

and then deltarune chapter one came out, and i felt the obsession all over again

it came to me in a very pivotal time in my life, as did chapter two, and chapters three and four. i cannot express to you enough how perfectly the timing of undertale and deltarune's releases were for me. and if i was going through a hard moment, and one of these releases hadn't just happened, i would replay undertale all over again. if i wasn't replaying, i was listening to the soundtrack. i don't think it's raining somewhere else was one of the songs that i listened to the most, but it definitely meant a lot to me. i can't explain how i felt hearing it in the game this morning. i didn't cry then. i was in shock, i had just watched chapters three and four deliver more than i ever thought they would, with the knight reveal and soul things and titan fight 

once i got to the latter half of chapter four i kept holding my breath because i felt like it could end at any moment. it was worth the wait but i had waited so long that i didn't want to let go again. there have been times especially recently where i've gone through rough patches and knowing that there would be a continuation soon of my favorite story in the entire world really helped to keep me going. i'm still not ready for deltarune to end. i don't want to be at the halfway point, i want to keep theorizing and being in a state of not knowing forever

but somehow, this track makes that lot a little more okay, a little more manageable, it makes the short wait for chapter 5 in 2026 (wow!) feel so much shorter, which is a good and a bad thing

i didn't cry hearing this track in the game but i'm sobbing now, i understood what it meant to me in that moment, it felt like a sense of genuine closure, it reminded me that it really was just ten year old me playing this game because despite everything, i'm still me, and i'm everything that undertale and deltarune has taught me and given me and more. loving something this much feels inherently bittersweet, because i'll never be able to experience undertale for the first time again, i'll never experience the moments where it came to mean so much to me ever again and that makes me so sad. how beautiful it is to feel completely destroyed by something because you love it so much

stories.author: @semidecent8008
stories.text:
And when the song played, suddenly I was 12 years old again. Cozied up on the couch watching a playthrough of Undertale, eyes wide and hands bouncing in excitement of the incoming Mettaton fight. Riding the school bus in the following weeks. suffering through mental health issues and planning to disappear from the world before high school because “no one cares unless you end it in middle school, by high school it’s predictable.” With Its Raining Somewhere else as the backdrop.

But I didn’t end up following through. Thank god. I just sat with those thoughts, as if they were normal. Then, Deltarune Chapter 1 came out. I was in high school, same age as the Fun Gang. Friendships came and went, the pandemic happened and caused me to be locked in my room and socially isolated. I was scared, I didn’t know if I’d ever have enough mental fortitude to build a future for myself, much less one I could count on. Sometimes I felt like Susie, angry and frustrated while hating every asset of myself. Sometimes I felt like Kris, like I wasn’t in control of my own life, a slave to instant gratification and escapism.

And then, a few days ago, I sat in front of my laptop, playing Deltarune and watching this scene play out. Bought with the money from my first real job in my field, sitting with the fact that my senior year of college is beginning. I’ve been through relationships, friends, medication after medication. Finally got my drivers license at the ripe old age of 20! Things aren’t perfect, and I have a lot of work to do in undoing the damage my depression caused my body.

But just for a moment, it felt like I was giving my younger self a big warm hug. Telling her that we made it. People do love you, and they would miss you if something happened. So if anyone reading this has been in a position like this, or is currently in a position like I was when Undertale came out: I hope you know how strong you are inside. You deserve love and comfort, but even when life won’t provide it for you, you’re strong enough to fight for what you deserve.

stories.author: @Nominitro
stories.text:
When I first got Undertale, I didn't really think much of it at first; I was young, why would I? I didn't understand the implications of my actions or how anything ties together, but I enjoyed the game, and that was apparently enough for me back then. I never really did pacifist when I first had the game on my Nintendo Switch Lite, as I wanted to fight Sans so bad, as one would. I loved Undertale, I loved it so much, it was one of my favorite games, I never stopped playing it or talking about it. When I did neutral one time, I went on that date with Sans, and the song "It's Raining Somewhere Else" began playing. I loved the song, and when the scene ended, I went on about my business, unaware this song would stick with me for so long. I never wanted it to end... but that's not how things work. All good things must come to an end, and so did Undertale.

However, when I saw that Deltarune was a thing and the first (or the additional second) chapter(s) where/was out, I had to get it. I wanted something like Undertale again... but it wasn't the same, but that doesn't mean I didn't like it. I loved it too, just as much as I loved Undertale. I played through the game, enjoying every second and every humorous line of dialogue. I was happy to see so many familiar faces, and I'm not gonna lie, it kinda hurt when Sans didn't recognize me, but I knew it was intentional game design and it meant no harm. I also enjoyed seeing new faces... but then that came to an end too.

Eventually, I got a laptop, and you know one of the first games I got on it... Undertale. I wanted to replay the game for so many reasons, and so I did. Neutral, Genocide... and yet no pacifist. I eventually got tired of playing the same routine over and over, and so I resorted to Undertale mods: Gaster Blaster Every Second, Purple Soul Boss Rush, etc. But one mod stood out: Undertale Together. I played through the game with my friend, and that was the first time I actually did pacifist. It was a new experience, one I wasn't quite used to. Battles weren't really an issue, as I had memorized the bullet patterns from my years of experience. It was fun, it was new... but I had already known what would've happened as we completed the route, since I already watched pacifist playthroughs many times before. 

Years of nothing new, the same old game, the same old endings, the same old dialogue. Then I got an idea after I heard Deltarune chapters 3 and 4 were coming out. I would replay Undertale and Deltarune on my Nintendo Switch Lite, which I had ended up finding. I played Undertale again, but this time... on a pacifist route, the one route I never completed on that device. It felt so relieving , so fulfilling. Finally, I had completed something I never correctly did. I replayed Deltarune, reliving old memories like I wanted to. I did Snowgrave, which was something I never had done properly before either, and that also felt so rejuvenating.

After a few more weeks... there was Deltarune, back and alive, Chapters 3 and 4 were finally here. I was excited, and had bought both of them on my laptop, ready for a new experience. It was fun, but it didn't feel like the Deltarune I had once known, it just felt like another fangame to be honest. Sure, the throwback with the Froggit projectiles in Chapter 3, the old Toriel sprite and fight aiming sprite in chapter 4. But it still didn't feel like Deltarune. It didn't feel like the old game. It didn't feel canon to the game's lore... 

Until I beat Chapter 4, and I heard that first cord. (As I was typing that previous sentence, I got chills down my spine.) That first chord made me freeze. It took me a second to process what just happened, or if that even did happen. Then came the second chord, next came the third, I knew I wasn't imagining things anymore. I actually heard those notes right. I didn't need the main melody to know what song this was, as I knew it by heart. Memories came flooding back, as I just looked at my laptop screen in utter disbelief and nostalgia. My eyes teared up, a smile brought to my face. Only then, did it feel like the canon Deltarune.

stories.author: @OverTheFullereneshif
stories.text:
I once had someone very important in my life. This person came into my life when I was going through a difficult time of social anxiety and isolation. I didn't have much of a social life and generally spent all my time alone, because it was the only thing I knew. This person was there for me for a long time, kept me company, and taught me what it means to trust someone deeply. To this day, this person knows me better than anyone else, better than my closest friends, better than my family.
It's been almost a year since that person left my life. I've been dealing with the grief and nostalgia all this time; I still can't believe that this person is gone and will probably never come back again. 
I listened to this song a lot when that person was in my life. Somehow, this person made everything feel alive, made things meaningful. This song reminds me of rainy evenings when I would talk to him.

This song has a huge impact on my world, at least. The impact is not directly related to the game, but I still have a lot of affection and feelings for this theme. 

He will probably never know that I still write these things about him.
