stories.author: @elliottlava7784
stories.text:
During his date, in this moment, in this exact point in timespace, far, far away, sans is happy. He's dancing with toriel, not yet cursed with forbidden knowledge. Ironically, the ones cursed with forbidden knowledge are deep within something that his associate would, in the universe he's talking to you in, recreate and succumb to. Right now, far, far away, he's with the person he was talking to through the door, he's loved, he's just a normal guy. And outside, it's raining. Somewhere else again, it's "raining." The entire underground is starting to go silent. A single human has wiped out their entire species and he's the last line of defense. Somewhere else sans is desperately trying to rebuild a machine, losing hope on ever going back to the place where he was happy. Trying to keep papyrus distracted as to not alarm him. In yet another timeline, sans is looking onto the sunset with all of his newfound friends. However, he knows this moment of respite won't last and he dreads what comes after the next reset. Somewhere else still, sans is with 3 people you don't recognize. They take a picture, and he writes a note by it. 
"Don't forget." 
In another, sans is nothing more than a pile of dust. What he doesn't know, however, is that the person who caused all of this joy, sadness, grief and laughter in all of those different worlds is the same one. And they're the child sitting right infront of him. The child that, for sans, is a clueless kid playing UNDERTALE for the first time, trying to understand what sans is saying, wondering how he came to be. Sans, during UNDERTALE, is extremely knowledgeable, while you, the player, are only beginning to scratch the surface. Sans during DELTARUNE, however, is still clueless, still innocent, still having people he loves, while the player, now 10 years after having last seen him, is almost omniscient. By the time you reach Chapter 4, you've already dissected every line of dialogue, every bit of hidden code, every secret, every cryptic post from 2012, everything. And sans inadvertently sparked the curiosity that would later create the mysterious character he remembers vaguely from back in Deltarune, "Kris Dreemurr", or more specifically, their SOUL. The player. You.

stories.author: @unprompted.autotomy
stories.text:
Maybe this'll just stay buried in the comments section but I feel like this moment was when I finally, finally understood Sans' struggle. I feel like the callback to Undertale here is extremely intentional, not just narratively but thematically. I spent the night trudging around Hometown reminiscing about my time with the game, about the days surrounding it and the friends I made and fun I had. It was a somber, wistful moment, sure, but it made me happy.

Walking in on Sans and Toriel, palling around without a care in the world cut through all that tension like a hot knife through a stick of butter. In the moment, I felt for Kris and Susie. In the moment I may have been just as hurt as them... but then I put together that, this was the moment Sans had always been yearning for in Undertale. This was the very thing he had tried, and failed, so hard to return to, for all that time. And it hit me... that I was in that very same position. That, looking around at the state of this cruddy, unkempt room I've been in since those very days, perhaps the happiest moments of my life were far behind me now, and there was nothing I, nor anyone else could do about that.

"you must really wanna go home. i know the feeling, buddo."

stories.author: @reysinx3345
stories.text:
Never in my life have I felt a massive sense of shock from a single note of a song. 

I was marathoning my way through both Chapter 3 and 4 when they dropped, nearing 11 hours before finishing Chapter 4's dark fountain and leaving the Church. Still trying to process everything the past hours of story only to be hit with that oh so familiar piano note. No further context was needed, Toby had told a story nearly a decade in the making from a single note in a song, and all of it came rushing at me like a train without any brakes installed. 

People praise Toby's writing and abilities as an artist a lot as they rightfully should. However, if a composer is able to tell such a substantial connection and plot point from a single note, I think that makes them special, incomparable to most others. The amount of planning and foresight needed in order for this song to hold as much weight as it does to someone who has kept up with Undertale and Deltarune since it began nearly a decade ago is nothing short of a masterclass.

Thank you, Toby Fox

stories.author: @Rocco049
stories.text:
You’re driving through the countryside on a humid night. The sky is covered by clouds, but the pale sliver of the moon is just visible through the haze. Your home is just over the next hill, around the next corner. You come to a stoplight. There is nobody around but the light stays red. You look through your window at the empty field to your left as the humidity finally gives way to the first drops of rain.

As you watch, the rain falls harder, beginning to cover the ground and the streetlight in a reflective sheen. You can see the red traffic light reflected in the street. 

As you sit there in the quiet, waiting for the light to change, a tune rises from your memory. You’re not sure where you know it from, but it’s familiar. Comforting. The light finally turns green but you hesitate. The song continues in your mind, mingling with memories of happiness, calm, and sorrow. 

The light turns red once more, leaving you to stay for another moment

In the place where it rained.

stories.author: @awakener-s3l
stories.text:
These scene is so uncomfortably realistic, despite being a meme.

Susie is all but states to have…. a rough home life. She doesn’t want to go home, telling Kris ‘Let’s go to your house’ if you try to take to hers. It’s also implied that, since moving to Hometown, she’s looked up to Toriel, and felt safe around her. When she was new to town, crying on the graveyard bench, she took her to the diner and fed her. When bullying Kris, Susie specifically mentions Toriel for her kindness. In ch 2, Toriel offers to let Susie sleepover, and while many of their interactions are *awkward*, they aren’t outright bad. As a result of this, in ch 3 and 4, one of Susie’s main motivations is finding and rescuing Toriel. So imagine what she must be feeling in this moment; she was almost killed by a eldritch creature of darkness, her mentor is forever dead, Ralsei’s been keeping secrets, she’s chilled by The Final Prophecy, and they’re no closer to stopping the Knight. And after all of that, coming home to the *one* place she feels safe and at home, even more so than her own house…. And she finds Toriel drunk and falling over, dancing with a complete stranger. Yea, no *wonder* she’s so quick to leave. I’m almost glad we don’t see the confrontation after, that can’t have been pretty.

She's just here, drunk and partying with someone she barely knows, seemingly not thinking of them at all. Not even asking why they're getting back so late.
Not only that, but Toriel seems to have forgotten about them ever since the rain started, which could've ended very badly since it was a tsunami. If they hadn't been in the Dark World Kris might've been locked outside for who knows how long.
It also likely isn't the first time Toriel's gotten drunk in front of them given their reaction.
Then there's Sans, while I don't think he and Toriel are gonna be a thing, it must suck to see someone who isn't your dad dancing with your mom. Especially someone who you barely know and has been a bit of a prick to you.

When I finished and got to this part I had to stop to cry and process everything I was feeling.  To tell the truth when I played Undertale for the first time 10 years ago I was in a very difficult stage of my life and it was one of the few things that drove me to stay alive. From then on I carried that philosophy about determination with me, I remembered it and kept it in complicated times, and well, now after 10 years I find myself in a very dark place again, a place where I seriously rethought everything again, because that's life, when you think the ugly part is over, something horrible comes and happens and so on. Although in reward Deltarune came and reminded me of what I was beginning to forget, that you have to be determined and you have to persevere especially in these moments when it seems that nothing makes sense anymore. This game comes along again and gives me a hand at a very difficult time in my life. Yes, in part it makes me feel very sad because of the nostalgia, because it make me think about everything I lost, in all the ones I lost since I played Undertale until now, but also, that message that spoke that we must find and maintain hope even when it seems that our destiny is written, everything that this game made me feel reminded me again why I must not give up and why it is worth staying alive.

stories.author: @thegoldenblob69
stories.text:
Something I realized.

So, Kris's family is divorced, their brother's off to college, and their relationship with the Holidays have long since faded - what with Dess missing/dead and all. 

But, then there was the girl.

Susie is new, she moved in some time ago. 

Darkners, are objects, toys, entertainment. Physical toys (cards, board games, etc), Laptops (internet/offline), TV (local, movies, etc), Church is all about community (plus free juice) and so that's another opportunity to connect with people.

'Darkners,' help lightners connect and understand one another. You and your friends get together to do a school project, but end up goofing off on the public library computer instead. Your friends crash out at your/their place and watch TV into the night. You and your friends might simply go to church, even if they arent super religious, just to have a community (and drink fruit juice).

Susie, by being new and not knowing the deep history that runs in the town, is able to rekindle that bond between everyone. Susie is the one bring Kris to places, talking to Noelle when no one else is around, giving a one to one with Ralsei, heck, even giving a damn about berdly one time. 

She is a new friend. If anyone has experienced bouts of loneliness or struggles making friends, having that one person, that single person, just suddenly appear in your life, can make a huge difference. Just someone who gets you, someone who feels for you and is always there. 

For Kris, it might be due to basically being alone for who knows how long. Holidays rarely come over, their dad is practically in rags, their mom is an alcoholic who only sees "her child" and not Kris, and their brother is at college. None of the other kids or other adolescents connect with Kris in any meaningful way. Then there's Susie, who connects with Kris, and is hanging out with them in ways they probably havent done or felt similar to in years.

Noelle's older sister, December, is either missing or dead. Carol is an overworked, harsh, and strict mother. Rudy is in the hospital, possibly on his deathbed. Noelle, for most of her childhood and adolescence, has lacked that older, more mature figure in her life. Rudy jokes too much while Carol, in the rare instances shes actually home and not working, is a total 180 and is way too harsh. Dess more than likely was the grounding figure. She hit Kris with a wiffle bat when they scared Noelle as kids. 

Susie, during the "mouse" seen, very much acted like that mature, and down to earth figure that Noelle has desperately been missing in her life thus far. 


The Legend makes it seem like their life, for both Kris and Noelle, is just the way things are. Kris's parents are divorced, Noelle's older sister, Dess, is gone. Nothing will be the same.

Then, there was the girl. Love finds its way to the girl. Susie warms up to her new friends, realizing this is not going to be like last time. She wont be a bully, she wont just move this time. She'll have friends now. 
Kris isnt going to be just the weird kid, they're not going to be lonely and misunderstood/lack connection forever. They'll have friends. Noelle's older sister, Dess, is still out there. We will find her. Even then, Susie is there for Noelle. Noelle will get stronger, and she will have Susie to help her break out her shell and grow into a better person. Berdly... uh... he'll learn hubris.

On a serious note, given Berdly's behavior in the Library in Chapter 4, I genuinely have high hopes for him. It seems he's on the path to becoming a better person. He acts like a chill and even empathetic dude once he no longer has that smarty know-it-all attitude. 

Still, I believe the main plot of Deltarune thus far is: Making new friends who connect with you and hanging out with them in various ways can help change your fate as a person. Time is always changing.

(I'm not including US, the soul, because thats another can of worms. Love is very much also referring to us gaining more and more control over Susie each chapter in some capacity. I really hope we dont fully possess her like we do with Kris. 

ALSO CAN WE GET OUR VESSEL?!?! (pls)

stories.author: @qewqieqie
stories.text:
Hi. 

I know its weird to comment on a OST video for this. Like they arent even real, so I'm not really talking to anyone, really. 

But, happy (albeit late, I encountered these guys somewhere in July 2025) one year to Mike/the Mikes & Tenna, for changing my life. I hold these fun guys quite dear to my heart. Them and Tenna, I've immensely enjoyed their dynamics, be it what we've seen ingame and what's been implied, and what ever else we can infer. Before came December 2025, I had no idea just how much content these 4 would have.(Note: Sorry I'm sneaking Tenna in that number as it was because of Tenna, I was even intrigued for who "Mike" even was. Even if fake Mikes weren't what I expected to meet, I swore to love whoever "Mike" turned out to be... and the interesting relationship Mike and Tenna grew to have.)


What an interesting bunch of characters. I remember thinking, "I'm digging myself a hole for liking these (apparently, cause I thought Mike would be more popular at first,) one-off characters. I can't believe they aren't more involved! Aren't they Tenna's main guys?" I was ready for the worse. I braced myself for enjoying these guys in my lonesome... 

It's... I still remember, the April 2026 Fangamer merch drop. My shock at the Mike shirt. And that Tenna pin. All together. It felt like, in that moment, every daydream and idea I had of these 4 had come true.


Even today, Tenna and the Mikes may not have the healthiest or fun dynamic now... I still like to pretend. Mike, and by proxy the Mikes, being Tenna's ???-in-command(higher than the first, being the Weather Duo, thats for sure)

I really love the Mikes and Tenna! Not a day goes by I don't think of them. The 'what-could-be' drives me nuts. What's Tenna relationship with Small Mike? Even more, Cowboy Hat Mike? Is the former a more professional feeling? The latter, more lax? Tenna called Mike a jokester, once, and usually its ZapperMike who's the funniest; is that Mike's playful side? Is Small Mike particularly strict? Are the requests he fulfills for Tenna, the ones demanded by his boss, or gifted to him; Did he give his boss princess treatment by his own suggestion!??!

Cat Mike, or Pluey, I'll call him Pluey since that's what he prefers. What kind of dynamic does he and Tenna share? The recent cutscene implies he's a comfort to Tenna. I find it quite endearing. But also, imagining that Mike carrying out Mike-like duties alongside the other two, is a jarring, yet incredible visual. I think a common interpretation of Pluey is that he doesn't carry out "Mike" duties at all, but I kind of relish the visual of Pluey barking out orders and tending to Tenna the same way Small Mike or Cowboy Hat Mike would.

Speaking of Cowboy Hat Mike, I know the meta of it, the cowboy likeness is a reference. But, I find it amazing just how much that and other characteristics they share in common with Tenna. Tenna has his own cowboy show, and Cowboy Hat Mike is a remote, technically making him closest to Tenna in terms of object. I just think that's often overlooked. But I get it, Cowboy Hat Mike probably isn't Tenna's remote... But if they were, that's be really cool, wouldn't it!?

Green Pippins... why the devotion to Tenna? It's really interesting to look into this. Most interpret his obsession to who Mike as his main drive for playing Mike, but that's hardly any of the Mikes' concern at all. Green Pippins(& by extension the other Mikes) is more of an actor than he is a conspirist. He drops the whole "who is Mike" thing immediately after beating him and the other two in their fight, so. The theory board, I believe it was just a way to discover who Mike is, not because he's trying to undercover who the real Mike is, rather, he's done it as a way to identify the real Mike and drag his ass all the way back to TV World so Tenna could stop mopping(as he originally did when a Mike wasn't present) and have Mike do his "Mike" job instead.


I wonder, I wonder all the time; From a story perspective, why do the Mikes want want to remain as Mike!? Ive seen interpretation that the Mikes don't enjoy carrying out Tenna's orders, but... I don't think thats true. I think theres a thing that co-exists, the Mikes *like* being Mike; in that way that they like(?) helping Tenna out, and the general feeling of the persona. I know that Pluey likes his. So, the other two could very well.

The Mikes dynamics are interesting as well. I really really really really reaaaally cherish that sprite artwork of Cowboy Hat Mike and Pluey playing cards. What Ive picked up‐ and again im ready to brace for change- is that Cowboy Hat Mike cant really interact with Pluey. The Zapper often forgets the Shadowguy's existence in the fight, makes me believe a few things, like Zapper doesn't understand Shadowguy speech(So far only Tenna and the Green Pippins have only been shown to understand them... as far as I know), and then they dont often run into each other between shifts. So I'm a little entertained to see them playing cards when they have little method of communicating with each other. So, maybe its through the Green Pippins that theyre connected. After all, he needed more Mikes, so he gathered more Mikes.

...But what consitutes a "Mike"? If Green Pippins doesnt believe Mike can be a cat, or even a cowboy, what the hell even is Mike? He's a more unreliable narrator than Tenna.

There's no way Tenna is this blind. Clearly, the Mikes are all distinct. But maybe, just maybe, hes amused by the act, and keeps them around because of it. It isn't common that he sees such diligent workers...

...

I really love the Mikes and Tenna. Ive only scratched the surface of what I think about them daily. In my mind, there's a perfect world where all 4 go on Looney Tunes esque wacky adventures and hang out either all together or duo(mike&tenna) style. It really warms my heart. I haven't had a workplace dynamic Ive enjoyed this much since who the hell knows when. I find it endearing that Tenna cherishes Mike as he does. I find it endearing that the Mikes keep up being Mike, or atleast the Green Pippins does, for the sake of Tenna. This strange, push and pull dynamic(push being the Mikes when theyre not Mike, pulls being Tenna requesting for Mike, and I cant lie I only just made that up), of a group of guys where one thinks is just him and his (singular) pal. What an interesting group.


Thanks to whoever made Tenna and Mike implied good... I'll call it acquaintances. Weirdos. I have no damn clue what Mike and Tenna see each other as. Friends, hopefully.

Haha. Hahahahaha. Um. Happy late one year anniversary to these 4 corrupting my mind. ...Maybe I'll add on more later. But I'm a bit tired from pouring my heart out and this is probably like only ~20% of it :') If theres typos...IDGAF!!!!! have a Mike&Tennaful day whoever is the poor soul who reads this this was meant to be like 3 sentences only lmfao

stories.text: Deltarune has been such a surreal experience for me. Outside of the dark world and RPG stuff, sticking straight to the light world and everything going on in Hometown reminds me so much of my childhood. I used to live in a neighborhood where my parents knew every adult on the block. They were social butterflies and had many friends. Before I was even born my sisters had made friends with most of the neighborhood kids. By the time I was born my friends (whom I still know to this day) held me when I was barely old enough to even open my eyes. I guess it's safe to say the name of the neighborhood since literally none of us live there anymore, but growing up in Hersand Court felt a lot like hometown. Being able to go outside and play with every neighborhood kid and being able to go to school with them in those days, it makes seeing Hometown and Kris' interactions with everyone instantly brings me back to those sanguine days. I miss them. All of them. We've all long since moved out of that neighborhood (hell I don't even live in that state anymore) but in spite of it all I'm just beyond grateful to have met and grown up with them all. They mean more to me than anything else life could possibly give me. Thank you Toby for indirectly allowing me to relive those days again through Kris.

stories.author: @primecuron402
stories.text:
General, crazy theorizing here, but: 
It really seems like Deltarune could be a prequel to Undertale. If Sans is the same Sans from UT, then that would mean Deltarune happens before Undertale, right? Since he supposedly got the postcard from Susie in DR, as we now know. If Sans is later trapped, by choice or not, in UT, then maybe this postcard is one of the only pieces of physical memory left that he has from the DR universe. If so, it would make sense why the postcard in UT says "Don't forget", since Sans really cares about not letting the jumbled up timelines stop him from remembering what has happened before- as a way of honoring what occurred as well as being a form of control over the seeming lack of control he feels when the timeline keeps resetting. Then there is also the whole thing with “the place where it rained.” Right? However, the chronology of the tenses with the titles is interesting. "It's raining somewhere else" is in the present tense, as if in the current moment that we experience it in UT, it is also happening at the same time in DR? But then in DR, the title is "The place where it rained", as if it were referring to the event in past tense. That past tense of "rained" is what makes me think of DR being some sorta prequel, either literally or just in the sense of DR being what happened in the timeline before everything was changed or moved.

It would also make sense because, in Undertale, the residents of Snowdin claim that Sans and Papyrus just appeared out of nowhere and asserted themselves. Maybe Sans moved their entire house into Snowdin and just didn’t tell anyone. Some people think that whatever happens at the end of Deltarune, especially some sorta weird route, would cause the skele-bros to move universes. Although, this would complicate what happened to Gaster with the whole “falling into his own machine” thing. Maybe Gaster also ended up trapped in, or willingly having moved to, Undertale after the events of Deltarune, and the machine was his way of trying to harness determination again so he could regain control and rectify some wrong that he had failed to fix.

Or maybe Undertale *is* the Deltarune universe, but some major rewriting of the world’s entire logic happens at the end of Deltarune, transforming it into Undertale instead. In that case, Gaster in Undertale might be trying to undo or reverse everything by using the determination extractor, but it doesn’t work. He falls in, gets split across space and time, and becomes scattered through the world as a result. The rewriting of the world's logic could explain why the same types of characters exist in both worlds, but with noticeably different paths that they've taken in life and currently living in a different environment- with some things still the same (such as Asgore and Toriel splitting up being the same catalyst event, but with the exact reasoning being potentially different per each timeline). As well as this, if in the Undertale timeline, certain characters no longer exist, such as the Holiday family, it would explain why something like the dark worlds are no longer a thing- since the catalyst for them to exist doesn't occur anymore. It's then possible that Kris is DR's version of Chara, since they wear the same shirt, with the shirt being the similarity across world rewrites. 

What do you think?

stories.author: @ClaireS-op8id
stories.text: When I was in high school, I asked my crush to homecoming with a Deltarune-themed card, because it was his favorite game. We went to the dance, and even though my feelings were revealed to be one-sided, the memories of being happy while spending time with him remain. I know this sounds cheesy, but what Susie says to Noelle in this scene nearly brought me to tears, because it reminded me so much of how I acted as a teenager in love. I didn't always know what to say, how to say it, or when. But I knew, just like Susie, that being around someone I loved made my days better, and that I wanted, as much as I could, to make a world where they would want to stay.

stories.text:
The neat detail i like about it, is how it's titled "I guess i'm in love". Before the Festival, everyone except Susie, made a big deal about her going to hang out with Noelle on the Festival. Susie just thought it was a cool hang out between friends, but then, at the lake... when Noelle finally opens up, does Susie realize "Shit, she DOES have a thing for me. Maybe... i do too?".
That scene works because it doesn't straight up tell you "Ey, Suselle is canon now!", it shows you that they really COULD be together, but they're still a bit too early to really call it official. Remember, Deltarune takes place in a span of just few days, it makes sense from Susie POV, she'd still be a bit hesitant to go full ham. It's as the Prophecy said, "Love finds it's way to the Girl."

Regardless, i LOOOVED that scene soo much, even as someone who's not that big on romance, it was the sweetest and heart melting thing i've seen in awhile.

stories.author: @riolulover9784
stories.text:
I literally don't know if I can put into words how it felt to hear this for the first time. I screamed, I teared up, I called all my friends and yapped insesantly to them.

I remember the feeling I had listening to base Field all the way back in 2017. I remember it's magic, it's wonder, it's motivational push to keep me going on this new journey. I remember listening to rendition and rendition of it across multiple covers, I remember listening to Carlos's cover for the first time and feeling that same miraculous whimsy in my heart all over again.

And now, over half a decade later, I got to feel it one more time. When I thought I had seen it all, when I thought we had moved far, far past that magical incredible time.

The Field of Hopes and Dreams to me, represents the excitement we all had for Deltarune in it's purest form. The incredible feeling of seeing a shadowdropped follow-up to one of the greatest indie games of all time. That feeling of being lost all over again in a beautiful world, strange, unfamiliar. I've gone through so much since then, and will no doubt go through more. 

To know that, in a sense: some piece of that part of my life has followed me all the way here to my present is..the greatest reassurance I could ever ask for. Like some impossible sign of fortune that despite everything, I'm still here.

Happy new Chapter guys. And thank you Toby for making me incredibly emotional at 11:34 in the morning.

10/10 would cry again

stories.author: @emmasalt88
stories.text:
I loved playing through these chapters so much, but by far what's stuck with me the most is how much I loved meeting the flowers. It's been said before but it's like meeting old friends you never knew you had- in Undertale they were always in the background, they help us during Neutral/True finale, and if you weren't super deep in the fandom, you never thought too much about these guys.

In Undertale all six non-flowery flowers have passed away by the time we visit. Only by Asgore's dedication to keep them alive (which mirrors Asgore's commitment to killing the humans in Undertale, interestingly) do we get to meet them, for just a single day. Brought back from the dead, like Gerson in ch.4 - long enough to live on in our memories, but short enough that we regret it couldn't be longer.

If we go back to Undertale, knowing what we do now, there's a few interesting things I'd like to point out-

Notably, Green made it the farthest out of the 6 flowers. Their equipment being found in Hotland means their commitment to kindness carried them farther than the others, but that willingness to sacrifice themselves meant they would never get a chance to leave the underground.

Yellow's equipment is sold in MTT resort, but Catti & Bratti mention finding their wares at the Waterfall dump. Meaning, both Yellow & Blue died in Waterfall, but far enough apart that they couldn't rest together.

Seth's equipment is sold by Gerson, which I like to think means they became friends during their journey. Seth learning under Gerson's care, until some day the worst came to pass.

Orange's equipment is sold in Snowdin, meaning she either succumbed on the way through the forest, or remained in Snowdin, unwilling to brave the crossing.

stories.author: @huangkeqi8263
stories.text:
I played Chapter 5 pretty much on the same hour as it released.

Man, I don't even know where to begin. It's been quite some time since I wanted to write down my thoughts on it, but I really don't know what to say anymore, after the sheer roller coaster of emotions I've been through.

Let's start with the my favorite characters:

Flowery is genuinely just one of the most well written and respectable characters Toby has ever made. I regret doubting him so much. We didn’t deserve this hero. Even if he knows that his time is limited, He never stops to do the right thing. He knows that he’s gonna lose, but that doesn’t mean he won’t give his all to protect his friends and make people like Ralsei realize they can be happy too. Some people called him a fraud for losing to the knight, But the fact that he risked his life just for a slim chance to save his best friend is already a proof of his bravery. Flowery tries to paint himself as an all powerful perfect hero, but in reality he’s the weakest entity that is nonetheless trying his hardest, and got so far because of his genuine love.

Out of all the flowers though, Aqua is easily my favorite. Within a myriad of characters with complex motivations and traumas, Aqua is defined by her simplicity and purity. She’s so innocent to the point that she doesn’t even understand what being hurt is like, and never holds any grudge against anyone who hurt her. but despite how much of a chaotic gremlin she is, She is still kind with everyone she meets, and just has that primordial good in her that makes her so endearing. When she waves goodbye to us, she doesn’t even think that we might not meet her again, which is especially touching and heartbreaking. She‘s such a cool character that could have stayed around for more humorous and cute moments, but it’s her ephemerality that made her so special.

The love and purity of all the flowers, how they would do so much to repay one man’s kindness, and how they don’t worry at all about going back to being flowers again, because even if they even managed to make Asgore truly happy for one day, it’s enough. Even the most insignificant and short-lived beings can become true heroes.

Who would have expected a story about flowers to be just as beautiful as them? Although they only truly got to live as humans for one day in their lives, their lives. managed to shine much brighter than even most “real” humans out there. A sunset is transient, but its beauty stays within you.

Toby Fox’s writing just feels so incredibly honest with itself, and so empathetic to all the characters involved. This game always made it a point how Darkners have dignity as people too, but the Flowers further exemplified this to the maximum. It isn’t like most other instances of the “dream world” trope I’ve seen, where everyone is fake and you shouldn’t be attached to them, making everything feel pointless and empty in the end.

I really would do anything just for the flowers to come back during chapter 7, and somehow get a chance to live happily. I know that it might make their goodbyes less impactful, but I didn’t even think about such things. I just want the best for them. This is a testament to how they successfully made me so emotionally invested in the flowers.

People say that this chapter is too lighthearted, but throughout the entire chapter I’ve felt especially heavy. Something about the whole atmosphere, the beautiful field and sunset, truly made this feel like we are nearing the end of the happy times. This isn’t just “another fun adventure” like Chapter 2 and 3. This truly felt like the “Last fun adventure”.

I am so genuinely shocked that people think this chapter doesn’t live up to the previous one, considering it topped chapter 4 for me in pretty much every aspect imaginable. Mind you, chapter 4 was already a masterpiece.

Of course I could write a massive review about everything else that is amazing about this chapter, but all I want to say is, Thanks you, Toby Fox. For delivering such an amazing story. I will never forget about them. All those wonderful friends, even as flowers, still deserve the world and more.

Even when Chapter 6 and 7 releases, Chapter 5 will forever hold a special place in my heart. This game is truly something special. Chapter 5 wasn’t just “Enjoyable” for me. It literally changed the way I look at everything around me.

* Sunset of seven suns.

* Cyan Sun, one of the smallest.
* Emits light very intensely, you feel blinded looking at it.

* Orange Sun, the smallest one.
* You can barely notice it behind others, it looks embarrased of its small size.

*... It warms your heart looking at it...
* Its beautiful...

* It looks lost, it looks for its way, but has no eyes.
* Guided by Blue Sun.

* Gold Sun, biggest of them all.
* It holds every sun together, no sun gets into the dark.
* But without the suns around it...
* The light would ran low.
* Shadows would grow.
* It would feel cold.
* That's why other suns are with it in the dark.
* Together they are stronger.
* ...
* Sadly, giant suns never last long.
* Everyone will miss it, once it will die.
* But remember, its light will stay on the sky for millenia.

* Time to go home, princess.

stories.author: @kaponos
stories.text:
This shop really encapsulates “the thing” about dark worlds, darkners, and deltarune in general.

A sunset is beautiful in the moment: filled with joy, excitement, longing- all the emotions of the soul, but before you know it, it’s gone. A bubble on a needle.

Treasure this world, because tomorrow it won’t be here. Treasure the friends you make in the dark, because when the light comes on, they cease to be.

It was our flower friends this time but all darkners and dark worlds will share this fate eventually- the toys will go back in their box and the dream will have to end. We will only have the memory of that dream left.

The world of Deltarune too will be over some day, the story will end, and though you can start over at the beginning and relive these moments, these characters can't move forward with you.

The influence of Link's Awakening on Deltarune is obvious, chapter 3 basically shouts its visual and musical identity at you, chapter 5 however pushes its themes. As the wind fish says: "Verily, it be the nature of dreams to end... Only the memory of this dream land will exist in the waking world. Someday, thou may recall this island.... that memory makes the dream real."

Our memories of Deltarune, of its characters and its world- our retellings and rewriting of its story into new wonderful things will be what keeps it alive. 

Art is what allows a sun to set forever.

stories.author: @bluekirby8194
stories.text: Also, y'all will hear a "shared" sample and go "ooh these MUST be the same song". Whatever crappy soundfont Toby took the harp (< actually its SGM_V2.01) from happened to take the same sample as what was used in Zen Garden (which is from Cakewalk TTS-1, which itself is just a reskin of Edirol Hyper Canvas, which is just the Classical set from the SD-90 (and SD-80 and SD-20) with some drums from the SC-88. And said harp sample is in a ton of Roland products. TTS-1 itself was actually deprecated a few years ago (due to legal rights) and is no longer included with any Cakewalk DAW. While I'm here and being pedantic, "soundfont" refers to a largely antiquated file type. NOT the "style" or "instrumentation" of something. In fact the file type was so largely antiquated that many, *many* DAWs just straight up do not have native support for them, and FL Studio only recently reintroduced support for them (which I've heard still kinda sucks), probably almost, if not entirely due to Toby Fox.

stories.author: @That1YtUser
stories.text: Tracks like this and Shop 3 remind me that we're closer to the end of this game then we'd like to think. As someone whose been following this game since Chapter 1 came out all the way back in 2018 (God, it feels weird knowing that was nearly 8 years ago at this point, felt like only yesterday we were all getting hyped for the next Smash Ultimate reveal trailer and Jevil was this fandom's darling character...), it's gonna be really weird when Chapter 7 comes out and there won't be anymore new chapters to get hyped for and probably not much to theorize or speculate about anymore. At the same time though, it feels awesome knowing I'll be one of those people who got to follow this games' development and releases and they happened. The people who play after all the chapters are out may get to experience it all in one go, but they won't really get the feeling of theorizing between releases and sitting with each chapter while waiting patiently to see where the story goes next. It really is a case of "you just had to be there".

stories.author: @terracottafred5126
stories.text:
Spoiler Warning:

This may sound silly, but I have a garden of my own. It’s something my mother and I have tended year after year since I was four.

That garden is everything to me. I weather each winter so that come spring I can see the pods starting to push their green shoots through the soil. So I can see green return to the Wisteria and the Peach tree and the Elephant Ears. So I can watch the grasses and clover start to retake the ground they lost before. 

But most of all, so I can see the flowers bloom again. The Roses, the Azaleas, the Sunflowers, the Daylillies, the Forget-Me-Nots. Each and every one of them coming back or being replanted, year after year, gives me something to look forward to. Knowing that soon my flowers will be back and they’ll need me and my mother to take care of them.

I think this chapter played perfectly into that attachment I have to my and my mother’s flowers. To see a story all about those flowers being given the consciousness to reciprocate that love just hit me right in my weak spot. And it made Flowery’s death at the end all the more impactful, reminding me of just how much it hurts whenever one of the plants I put so much time and love into just isn’t going to make it. All around beautiful chapter. Made me want to go and just lay down in the middle of the grass and smell the flowers and watch the bees buzz around.

Maybe once it stops raining

stories.author: @Microwave_guy

Man, the Flowery fight was so sick but sad;
The flowers were only supposed to live for ONE day, but they are at LEAST 18 years old. That's 6.5 thousand times more than what they were supposed to live. All that time, their caretaker was there with them and cared for them, giving them everything they wanted, until they were physically rooted to the table they were growing on.
Imagine thinking you were going to die in a garbage bin with your only purpose in like to be to look nice, but someone lets you live for 6.5 thousand lifetimes while giving you everything you've ever wanted?
Flowery doesn't want the Lightners to know the suffering they caused, or is misguided, or wants people to like him. He wants Asgore to know how grateful he is. He didn't even have a state of consciousness prior to the Dark World.
Given how the flowers are rooted to the table, and require light, and need the special care, they can't come to Castle Town and unless Kris' soul is around, he can't have another Dark World or even be in one for too long. Since the flower's consciousness came from the Dark World's effects, this is the only time Flowery will ever be able to express his gratitude or even feel.
One last thing, since the flowers require their special lights, they're actively withering away in the Dark World. Every second Flowery is existing, he's slowly dying from a lack of light. Even if Kris sealed Castle Town to keep Flowery's Dark World, he would eventually die either way.

stories.author: @popslyme
stories.text:
Call me crazy, but the colours of the silhouettes in this scene feels intentional. Maybe I'm onto something, or maybe spending a whole chapter with coloured characters that represent traits made me see patterns in places there aren't.


To start Asriel is coloured Green. In other chapters, people constantly praising him. He's always described as this popular kid who got along with everyone. When he goes to college, everyone seems to miss him. Green, the flower, also gets along with both the flowers and the fun gang through their kindness. From this, I don't think its unreasonable to assume that Asriel was also a very kind person.

Asgore, unsurprisingly, is more interesting. He starts out Yellow, representing his obsession with bringing justice to the Knight that we see throughout scenes in Flower Castle. Being a police chief aswell means that Asgore's job would be to enact justice. But eventually, he became obsessed with doing so to prove his sanity.
Others also pointed that the character of Yellow could also reflect his inner self-hatred, which Asgore himself talks about while his silhouette is yellow.

But Asgore then turns Red. This could mark a turning point, perhaps when he was demoted from being police chief. But I moreso see it as the point where he abandoned the idea of enacting justice. When his obsession grew so much that he only wanted to prove that it wasn't his fault. He was determined. And that Determination ultimately hurt his family.

Kris is light blue, or aqua i guess. It seems like Kris was there during the event (seen as Asgore doesn't try to explain it to them). It makes sense that they would understand his actions better, and be more patient with Asgore and willing to forgive him as a result.
Though the silhouette also shows Kris as a young child, so perhaps it shows patience and forgiveness through naivety, of a lack of proper umderstanding. Aqua also acts naive, so I don't think this is farfetched. It's just weird that the two possible explanations imply the opposite things. Makes my point feel weaker.
Edit: though its not impossible that Kris simply didn't understand when they were young, but then grew to understand as they got older. ig that could serve to explain both?? A patient character who is still willing to forgive after learning the truth much later on.

Finally, Toriel is Purple, and my explanation for her is more flimsy for this, but I do think it still works. Asgore's obsession drove him mad, but Toriel persevered. She didn't put up with his behavior, and left, perhaps for the safety of her children. She didn't let Asgore sway her own stance on things. Even in the present day (as seen in her conversation with Rudy in the church), she still stands against what he's doing.
See what I mean by this one being the flimsiest, or atleast the hardest to explain. She also does just wear purple often sooooo its hard to say with confidence.

The same goes for all of this really. It feels like im right, but theres obvious holes in my explanation. Maybe someone else could say it better, or maybe im just reading too hard into colours.

Anyway yap over

stories.author: @tcurt99
stories.text:
Fun fact! This song's file is called "Flowery_iog_extended.ogg" in the files. I wondered for a short minute what "iog" means before remembering it's an acronym for Illusion of Gaia. I did a bit of digging and found this track is in fact a reference to the song "Will's Dream/Deep Sadness" from it's soundtrack! Quintet's games all have what i can only describe as a fever dream like vibe to them so it makes sense that they would be a big inspiration for the Literal Fever Dream Game.

I have a bit of history with IOG... It was one of the only SNES games i had for a long period of time and one of the few i still have worth caring about. It had a deep impact on me despite the relatively short time i spent with it so much so that it influenced a dream i had. The dream was pretty normal all things considered. 
The plot was about Mario and Luigi being on the run and seeking shelter in a cave... The rest is either a blur or it petered out into nothingness until the end. The dreams end had clear gameplay. It was a top down dungeon crawler like IOG and Zelda It looked like an snes game. The final battle started out with Luigi vs... a Geodude? The room wasn't open and had many rock scattered around making it kind of maze-like. At the time the frame of reference would have been Brock's gym of mt moon from pokemon gen 1...
After Luigi defeated the Geodude the real final battle began with a boss that resembled a cross between Nightmare from Kirby's Adventure and Dark Gaia from IOG with a little bit of Lavos in there but i'm not sure if i was familiar with Chrono Trigger yet at the time.
The ending had Mario and Luigi save the day and beat the final boss but their efforts were never praised or remembered and instead their pursuer from the beginning was hailed as the hero instead who turned out to be... Yoshi? The music that played during this scene was Reprise from Spirited Away and i searched for the exact song for years and years before hearing it again and realizing it was the song from that dream.
I debated a bit on if this last bit is worth sharing, because i don't expect people to believe me, but the room before the final battle looked a lot like the room you fight ERAM in during CH3... I had this dream in 2008.

stories.author: @i-Sparki
stories.text:
My take is that the flowers represent as close as possible to the six Humans from Undertale. One has to remember, they were all kids in that game when the ended up Underground and thus would not perfectly embody their main trait. It would make a lot of sense that each of them was flawed in the sense of their main trait but still represented it best in their own unique way.

Aqua may be energetic and seemingly impatient but she has a burning curiosity to ask questions and persevere no matter how long it might take to get what she wants- from knowledge to play.
Seth may misunderstand a lot of what they read and learn but they genuinely learn from their mistakes and look out for the best in everyone around them through the one medium they know best: knowledge.
Yellow may be misguided on what justice actually is, to the point where he punishes himself, but he has a strong heart and unwavering passion to do right for others, especially his friends.
Orange may be insecure about her image and strength but she pushes past those insecurities with incredible courage and eventually learns to accept that being herself is more human than anything she could ever dream to be.
Green may be one to hold a grudge but she is a friend to all and would always be right there with food and an ear to lend. She never turned away the Fun Gang or any of the others, even if they made her mad.
Blue may be overly emotional but she was in touch with everyone else's flaws because of it, and thus was able to give heartfelt advice that they needed to hear, especially to Susie and Orange.

And Flowery may be eccentric and egotistical, twisting everything for selfish desires, he was also determined to show someone he deeply cared about an ideal world after seeing him suffer in cold isolation for years on end.

stories.author: @KraziShadowbear
stories.text:
I love Flowery.
While it's all for show, he was never malicious or heartless like Flowey was.
Even as a flower, inside, deep beneath all the illusions and facade, he was somehow just as "human" as the rest of the flowers were.

I didn't hate him. Even from the start. I was suspicious, yes, but wasn't really, fully read to "commit" to hating him until I'd seen what really was in his heart, underneath the facades.
Every time he looked like he was close to doing something truly "evil", he softened up and let go. Like a really actual loving human. He didn't even kill us in the final battle.
He was like the eldest brother to all the other flowers.
And now he's gone.

The way that bass line and rhythmic drums creep in right around when Flowery talks about the "darkness" underneath the town really stuck with me.
It gave me chills. It kind of reminded me of "The Dark Truth" track from Chapter 2.
It felt like one of the only instances where Flowery was being dead serious and pulled down all the facades.

I wonder what will happen in these next chapters after this "one last fun adventure" Toby was talking about.

stories.author: @commpisto5948
stories.text:
Flowery is dead. It's not a Tenna situation when he can be revived. Even if he would, he would stay a flower.
We will never meet him again. We will never meet all the flower characters we learned to love so much ever again. And if we do, it will be because the end of the world had come and the Roaring opened fountains across the town.

There is something so grim about not seeing the rest of the flowers ever again.
Flowery knowingly fought the Knight atleast, so he died with bravery.

But while a lot of the flowers were okay with sealing the fountain, others were not. Aqua was not even aware that this will be her last moment of conciousness. Hell, Orange literally cried as she thanked us for watching her dream.

The flowers, in the end, did not get to fulfil their own dreams. 
Aqua will never play again; Seth will never meet Berdly or learn everything; Green, while kind, will never be able to show his kindness again; Orange will never become the strong and brave fighter she wanted to be; Yellow will never serve our justice or have a moment with Blue again, and vice versa.

In his boss battle, Flowery literally did his best to fulfil all of his friends' dreams. He let Aqua play and Seth show his intelligence; he let Orange be brave and gave him space to attack by himself, and even green helped; he gave Yellow another moment to dish out justice and be with Blue.

Flowery fulfilled everyones dreams as much as he could, because his own dream was as selfless as it could be. The moment Asgore said to seal the fountain, Flowery agreed and let them. All of the flowers let it happen.

I don't think there is any character in Deltarune as noble and selfless as the flowers and Flowery specifically. Even Susie, the literal hero of the prophecy, would not be able to give up on her Castletown for the better. That's what it shows in the end of the chapter.

stories.author: @Official_Proxy
stories.text:
1st thought I had when we appeared outside was "What the hell happened to all the decorations, it's like the town got swept by a wind and nobody bothered to clean it up."
Then I remembered the mess that happened in the Church, caused by the Knight. And now I'm worried.

And yes, Susie considering Hometown her home was heart-breaking, because I bet even Ralsei knows it won't last forever. Ralsei tried to tell us not to get too attached to him because he's a darkner and his purpose is to serve, after all. It was the decision of us, the player, and Susie, that he became more than just a tool. Susie will have no home again once it's gone, that's most likely why she smashed the prophecy glass in ch4 that we didn't see. Ralsei was terrified that Susie will see it, because he knew that she would be unable to accept losing what she had built with Kris.

I just hope we get to beat some sense into her parents for neglecting her to a point where she'd rather sleep anywhere else but her home. Unless... she doesn't have a home to begin with? What do we really know about her parents?

Also, has anyone noticed the discoloration of Kris'es skin at the start of ch5? There are multiple references to him being actually dead, and apart from Susie having multiple lines where she says she "thought that he's dead" in multiple chapters on several occasions, the skin thing makes it look like Kris is losing his life power the longer the Player heart stays outside of his body. The lack of HP at the beginning would suggest that too, and I'm afraid it's only a matter of time before Kris turns into a goner, or a straight up ghost. I do hope there's a way to reverse it. Maybe the summoning ritual he did with Catti was supposed to summon a demon that made a pact with him to grant him more life essence? That's just my idea. It also explains the line "You were used up." from the perspective of the demon using Kris'es life essence until it runs dry. Or... maybe Kris is the only instance of a lightner and darkner in one, where the soul belongs to a lightner, but Kris is no longer alive, so he has to borrow Determination, which is very similar to the way Mad Mew Mew works (lightner ghost, darkner body). This would then further explain why Kris wants to make more fountains. Not only does it let him stay alive indefinitely while in one, he also gets to experience adventures with Susie, whom he wants to offer solace from her harsh life. It also also explains how Kris is capable of "changing shape" despite not possessing magic, like humans do. He lacks the magical power of a living human, because the soul is still unharmed (unabsorbed) by the body fully. And he can't afford to absorb it, because it would no longer provide him with a healthier life? Just a thought.

stories.author: @premieregoatboy
stories.text:
That last scene with Ralsei sneaking in that slice o’ cake at Susie’s bed really reminded me how much it parallels Undertale’s True Pacifist Route; and how important this chapter actually had been. The reason this chapter felt so self-indulgent and fanservicey. . .was because it was a culmination of Toby Fox’s desire and passion. The dream he had all those years ago finally came to fruition. The Sunset of Seven Suns that provided Chapter 5’s hope ten years ago, that inspired the seven SOULs in Undertale, that hope was finally realized this chapter. He dedicated an entire chapter to express his deepest dreams and desires, holding no bars back with unique gameplay styles, with so many fanservicey interactions, and every emotional moment that feels so powerful and compelling on its’ own—-like Toby celebrating his own dream. And expressing his gratitude for us watching it. . .

“Thank you for watching my dream.”

this ending brought me to tears. especially right after flowerys death. everything broke me. im really happy that susie and noelle are together but holy shit do i feel bad for kris. kris didnt stand there waiting for susie to make sure she was safe, they waited just for that slight chance that susie would come back and grab them to help set up. but in the back of their mind they knew it wouldn't happen. they walked away, head looking towards the ground in pure betrayal. their best friend, leaving them for love, with nearly no second thought. jesus christ. i want to hug kris so badly. i will give them the happy ending they deserve.

stories.author: @PetikG
stories.text:
First time. First time this game made me cry and it's the post-credit scene.

Or rather, this is the second time I cried. The romantic scene with Susie and Noelle was the true first one to make me cry.

I'm just so happy for Susie.

stories.author: @ZeroGraveT99
stories.text: I cried when I saw Kris walking away from the door after it is implied that they stood there for a while in silence and despair. I feel so bad for them.

stories.author: @VividbreadReports
stories.text: I was genuinely crying for the entire credits and cried harder when i saw susie in the darkworld without kris.

stories.author: @Charles1337-DR-Youtuber
stories.text: Seeing the after-credits scene with Susie all happy in Castletown and then Kris walking away with their head down is the fourth time I've ever shed tears to internet media from what I can remember.

stories.author: @jackhammer4499
stories.text: This isn't the first time something happened with the name of Scarlet Forest. There's cut dialogue of a quiz in Chapter 3 where Tenna asks the name of the forest, and Ralsei says something like "Scarlet Forest! Or is that the name of the music?" Or something like that. And considering the weird mistakes and forgetfulness around Scarlet Forest, and its trees being a symbol of THE FORGOTTEN MAN, I think there's something going on here.

stories.author: @IncomprehensibleBeing
stories.text: fuck man. Deltarune Chapters 3 and 4 came out during an incredible time in my life, the best I say. And here we are, a year later. It's not as good as it was. Lost a lot of friends along the way, but made a few new ones and reconnected with old ones. I love this game. The one constant through my life, no matter what.

stories.author: @The_Prince_From_The_Dark
stories.text: It might be the same soundtrack as in "Piano Collections, Vol.1" but after seeing THAT scene..? It just hits different and It's so good that it breaks my heart into pieces every time I hear it. 🥺

stories.author: @a77i
stories.text: I really love how the piano covers are complete reimaginings of the song rather then copying it entirely, also gets me especially emotional because of Kris and their connection to the piano, how it was one of the only things they seemed to be passionate about but can't play anymore, it's so sad. Also even sadder after hearing Toby talk about his disability, I remember him writing about how he could barely play the piano at all and had to use text to speech for everything in a newsletter, it's very heartbreaking and it's part of why Kris and their piano scenes in ch4 are some of my fav scenes in the game

stories.author: @spaghettisauceheadache
stories.text: i listened to this at 3 in the morning, in an almost pitch black room after finally getting deltarune and getting to play through the game and oh my god was it more beautiful than i could ever have imagined. this song feels like the perfect representation of how it feels to play deltarune for the first time.

stories.author: @Violet_The_Camerawoman
stories.text: This chapter... Tore me up so badly. The themes with Asgore, the motifs, the flowers... And Susie and Noelle. Kris as well. This game has had such a large impact on my life, and this chapter feels like a hopeful bookend, even though we still got two more chapters to go. Thank you so much, Toby Fox.

stories.author: @tcurt99
stories.text: I think this track being the last on the soundtrack cements why i love Flowery so much. The ending is such an emotionally charged experience and your likely to miss where this actually plays. I think back to how Reunited is the track i go back to when recalling undertale like those final moments are where the game always will be for me and so many other people. Our final memories of Flowery are weird pinups that are a reference to a game most deltarune fans will have never heard of in their entire lives. It's so absurd and i love it with every fiber of my being.

stories.author: @themememaster7844
stories.text:
I just gotta say I find it funny how other than chapter 1, each soundtrack release has like a redounding finale for its second to last song and then just jumpscares you at the end with a goofy song.

Chapter 2: well done you completed the chapter, see you again soon...oh by the way here's what berdly would've sounded like if he was any more full of himself.

Chapter 3+4: what a crazy secret fight with some interesting secrets huh? Anyways Kris wanted to play the piano for You.

Chapter 5: You overcame quite the ordeal, as did everybody else. Now that we have looked back on the sunset we must prepare for the journey ahead...oh by the way remember the image you saw with the BromideR? Yeah ill never let you forget it.
